How Much Cache Does Reasoning Need?
Depth–Cache Tradeoffs in KV-Compressed Transformers

Xiao Wang Email: FujianAI42@163.com
Abstract

The key-value (KV) cache is the dominant memory bottleneck during Transformer inference, yet little is known theoretically about how aggressively it can be compressed before multi-step reasoning degrades. We study this question through kk-hop pointer chasing under a shared KV cache of size ss, attention dimension mm, HH heads, pp-bit precision, and a locality-respecting cache controller (a minimal restriction satisfied by all standard KV-compression methods). We give three results.

(1) Product depth lower bound (conjectured). We conjecture that any such Transformer solving kk-hop pointer chasing on nn tokens (n≥4​kn\geq 4k, s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4) requires L=Ω⁡(⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉)L=\Omega\!\bigl(\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil\bigr), and we isolate the sole remaining gap as a specific probabilistic step on the joint distribution of the algorithm’s cache trace and the pointer chain (Open Problem 1). The product structure—cache reachability and per-window bandwidth multiply, not compete—is the central technical feature. We prove unconditionally (i) a matching upper bound L=O⁡(min⁡(k,⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡(2​s)⌉)⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)L=O\!\bigl(\min(k,\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}(2s)\rceil)\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil\bigr) via windowed pointer doubling, and (ii) the max-bound L=Ω⁡(max⁡(⌈k/s⌉,⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉))L=\Omega\!\bigl(\max(\lceil k/s\rceil,\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil)\bigr) on the full parameter range; closing the conjecture amounts to upgrading max\max to a product in the s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 regime.

(2) Bandwidth barrier. The product bound is quantitatively binding only in the narrow or low-precision regime (H​m​p≲log⁡nHmp\lesssim\log n). We formalize this limitation as a barrier theorem: any depth lower bound provable via per-window distinguishability counting—a class that includes reachability arguments, bandwidth arguments, and their combinations—cannot exceed ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil in the H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n regime. Breaking this barrier would require fundamentally different proof techniques, e.g., unconditional communication-complexity lower bounds for pointer chasing. We view this as a structural obstacle on the road to characterizing depth in standard LLM configurations.

(3) Sharp error behavior and adaptive–oblivious separation. Under random cache selection, we establish a two-regime characterization of joint success probability over T=⌈log2⁡k⌉T=\lceil\log_{2}k\rceil stages of windowed pointer doubling: with oblivious caches, Pr⁡[ℰ]≤(s/(n−T))T+2​T3/n\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\leq(s/(n-T))^{T}+2T^{3}/n (exponential decay in TT); with adaptive locality-respecting caches, Pr⁡[ℰ]=s/n\Pr[\mathcal{E}]=s/n exactly (matching upper and lower bounds), independent of TT. The resulting Ω⁡((n/s)T−1)\Omega((n/s)^{T-1}) separation quantifies why heavy-hitter eviction qualitatively dominates random eviction for multi-hop reasoning (Liu et al., 2025; Ananthanarayanan et al., 2026).

Together, these results give a sharp picture of what current proof techniques can and cannot establish for cache-constrained reasoning. The central open problem is to close the gap between the unconditional max-bound and the conjectured product-bound; we identify the specific technical step required and survey candidate routes for closure.

1 Introduction

As context windows in large language models scale beyond 100K tokens, the key–value (KV) cache has become the dominant memory bottleneck during inference (Shi et al., 2024). This has driven extensive work on cache compression through eviction (Zhang et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Cai et al., 2024), quantization (Liu et al., 2024), and merging (Wang et al., 2024); these methods report 8080–90%90\% compression with limited degradation on standard benchmarks.

Yet mounting empirical evidence shows that multi-hop reasoning degrades far faster than single-hop retrieval under the same compression rates (Ananthanarayanan et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2025; Cai et al., 2025). This raises a sharp question: how much cache must be retained for multi-step reasoning to remain possible?

We formalize this through kk-hop pointer chasing and study the depth required to solve it under a shared KV cache of size ss. Our main positive result is an unconditional max-bound lower bound, plus a conjectured product lower bound: cache reachability (∼k/s\sim k/s sequential windows) and per-window bandwidth (∼log⁡n/(H​m​p)\sim\log n/(Hmp) layers per window) should multiply rather than compete. We identify the precise probabilistic step (⋆)(\star) needed to turn the conjecture into a theorem and leave it as Open Problem 1; we also give a narrow unconditional partial result in the extreme low-precision subregime s⋅2m​p<8s\cdot 2^{mp}<8 under an additional query-only controller assumption (Remark 4.13). Our other main results (the matching upper bound, the bandwidth barrier, and the adaptive-vs-oblivious error analysis) are unconditional.

The product bound is, however, quantitatively binding only in a specific parameter regime—when precision is low or models are narrow enough that H​m​p≲log⁡nHmp\lesssim\log n. In standard LLM configurations (H=32H=32, m=128m=128, p=16p=16, giving H​m​p∼6.5⋅104≫log⁡nHmp\sim 6.5\cdot 10^{4}\gg\log n), the bandwidth factor ceilings at 11 and the bound reduces to the cache-reachability constraint L≥⌈k/s⌉L\geq\lceil k/s\rceil alone. This raises the natural question: can the product structure be sharpened to bind in the standard LLM regime?

Our second contribution answers: not via a broad class of current proof techniques. We formalize a barrier theorem showing that any depth lower bound provable via per-window distinguishability counting—a class that encompasses reachability arguments, bandwidth counting, and their combinations—saturates at ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil whenever H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n. The barrier is structural: multi-head attention (H≥2H\geq 2) makes per-layer bandwidth (H​m​pHmp) exceed per-token state capacity (m​pmp), so any counting-based per-window argument ceilings within a single layer. Breaking this barrier would require either translating unconditional communication-complexity lower bounds for pointer chasing (Nisan and Wigderson, 1993; Yehudayoff, 2020; Mao et al., 2025) into Cache-Transformer depth lower bounds without the MPC conjecture (an open problem) or genuinely different proof techniques.

Our third contribution is a sharp, two-regime analysis of error behavior under random cache selection, which partially explains the empirical “hallucination cliff” of Ananthanarayanan et al. (2026). The joint success probability of windowed pointer doubling over T=⌈log2⁡k⌉T=\lceil\log_{2}k\rceil stages admits qualitatively different scaling in two regimes: for oblivious caches (chosen without seeing π\pi), direct enumeration gives Pr⁡[ℰ]≤(s/(n−T))T+2​T3/n\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\leq(s/(n-T))^{T}+2T^{3}/n, exhibiting exponential decay in TT (Theorem 3.8). For adaptive locality-respecting caches, the joint probability is exactly s/ns/n, independent of TT, and is matched by an explicit “chain-tracking” controller (Theorem 3.9). The resulting separation, Ω⁡((n/s)T−1)\Omega((n/s)^{T-1}) between adaptive and oblivious, quantitatively explains the empirical observation (Liu et al., 2025) that heavy-hitter (adaptive) eviction qualitatively outperforms random or recency-based eviction on multi-hop reasoning tasks.

Contributions.
  1. 1.

    Product lower bound (Conjecture 3.1): We conjecture that for any locality-respecting controller, L=Ω⁡(⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉)L=\Omega(\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil), binding in the narrow-model regime. We provide (i) an unconditional max-bound L=Ω⁡(max⁡(⌈k/s⌉,⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉))L=\Omega(\max(\lceil k/s\rceil,\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil)) from reachability and output bandwidth, (ii) an identified proof strategy via exit-based distinguishability counting, reducing the conjecture to a probabilistic step on the joint distribution of cache trace and pointer chain, and (iii) partial progress closing the gap in sub-regimes.

  2. 2.

    Matching upper bound (Theorem 3.2): L=O⁡(min⁡(k,⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡(2​s)⌉)⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)L=O\bigl(\min(k,\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}(2s)\rceil)\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil\bigr) via windowed pointer doubling.

  3. 3.

    Bandwidth barrier (Theorem 3.6): Any per-window distinguishability-based argument cannot prove L=ω⁡(⌈k/s⌉)L=\omega(\lceil k/s\rceil) when H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n.

  4. 4.

    Three-part error analysis under random caches (Theorems 3.8, 3.9, Corollary 3.10): Under oblivious caches, Pr⁡[all T stages succeed]≤(s/(n−T))T+2​T3/n\Pr[\text{all $T$ stages succeed}]\leq(s/(n-T))^{T}+2T^{3}/n—exponential decay in TT. Under adaptive locality-respecting caches, the same probability is Θ⁡(s/n)\Theta(s/n), tight with an explicit construction. This gives an Ω⁡((n/s)T−1)\Omega((n/s)^{T-1}) separation between adaptive and oblivious, explaining why heavy-hitter eviction dominates random eviction empirically.

Relation to prior work.

Sanford et al. (2024) proved O⁡(log⁡k)O(\log k) depth suffices for kk-hop pointer chasing with full cache (s=ns=n), and Ω⁡(log⁡k)\Omega(\log k) is necessary under an MPC conjecture. Their analysis does not address cache constraints and assumes infinite precision. The two results are complementary: theirs is conditional and cache-oblivious; ours is unconditional (modulo locality) but finite-precision. In the s=ns=n limit, our bound gives L≥⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉L\geq\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil, which for H​m​p=O⁡(log⁡n)Hmp=O(\log n) matches Ω⁡(log⁡n)≥Ω⁡(log⁡k)\Omega(\log n)\geq\Omega(\log k); in larger H​m​pHmp, our bound is weaker and cannot recover their Ω⁡(log⁡k)\Omega(\log k), reflecting the bandwidth barrier. Peng et al. (2024) use communication complexity to prove a related inability of shallow Transformers to compose functions (e.g., grandparent lookup on a genealogy), giving unconditional impossibility for low-depth models on pointer-chasing-like tasks; their work focuses on depth vs. domain size rather than depth vs. cache size, and does not address KV compression. Haris and Onak (2025) prove a Θ⁡(n​d)\Theta(nd) space lower bound (for d=Ω⁡(log⁡n)d=\Omega(\log n); in the low-dimensional regime d=o⁡(log⁡n)d=o(\log n) they show Ω⁡(d⋅ed)\Omega(d\cdot e^{d})) for KV cache compression in attention-based autoregressive Transformers via a reduction from communication complexity, using a Johnson-Lindenstrauss-style construction; this is orthogonal to our depth-vs-cache tradeoff, focusing on whether sublinear space suffices at all rather than on the interaction between depth and cache size. The concurrent empirical study (Ananthanarayanan et al., 2026) independently observed phase-transition-like behavior in multi-hop accuracy under compression.

2 Setup

Definition 2.1 (Cache-Restricted Transformer).

An (L,H,m,p,s)(L,H,m,p,s)-Cache-Transformer operates on NN tokens under pp-bit arithmetic: every weight entry, every intermediate activation entering a subsequent layer’s input (queries, keys, values, attention-output vectors, and token representations) is drawn from a finite set 𝒬p\mathcal{Q}_{p} of cardinality at most 2p2^{p} per coordinate. The softmax attention weights themselves are computed in continuous arithmetic and are not required to be pp-bit quantized; only the attention outputs (the mm-dimensional vectors fed into the residual connection) are rounded to 𝒬pm\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m} before the next layer. Representations Xi(ℓ)∈𝒬pmX^{(\ell)}_{i}\in\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m} are indexed by layer ℓ∈{0,…,L}\ell\in\{0,\dots,L\} and token i∈[N]i\in[N]. At each layer ℓ≥1\ell\geq 1, attention is restricted to a shared subset S(ℓ)⊆[N]S^{(\ell)}\subseteq[N] with |S(ℓ)|≤s|S^{(\ell)}|\leq s. Tokens outside S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)} are strictly inaccessible at layer ℓ\ell: their key–value pairs are deleted and contribute exactly zero to attention. The subset S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)} is chosen by a deterministic function CℓC_{\ell} of all layer-(ℓ−1)(\ell-1) representations. Element-wise MLPs between layers are unrestricted in computation but their outputs are quantized to 𝒬p\mathcal{Q}_{p} coordinatewise before the next layer. For token positions jj that do not participate in attention at layer ℓ\ell (i.e., the query at position jj attends to no keys, equivalently the attention output at position jj is zero), we set Xj(ℓ)=Xj(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell)}_{j}=X^{(\ell-1)}_{j} (representation carried forward unchanged via the residual connection); this convention is standard and captures the behavior of evicted-token slots in KV-compression systems.

This induces a finite state space: each mm-dimensional attention-output vector takes one of at most 2m​p2^{mp} values.

Remark 2.2 (Modeling assumptions).

The finite-precision assumption reflects hardware reality: FP16, BF16, INT8 are standard, with p=8p=8–1616. The counting argument (Lemma 4.2) requires only that each coordinate lies in a finite set of size ≤2p\leq 2^{p}; floating-point formats such as BF16 satisfy this with p=16p=16, regardless of exponent/mantissa split. The hard cache boundary models physical KV cache eviction, where deleted tokens’ keys and values are removed from GPU memory. Our bounds do not apply to soft compression (value quantization, token merging) or to infinite-precision theoretical models.

Remark 2.3 (Per-head cache budgets).

Definition 2.1 assumes a shared cache S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)} across all heads. If instead each head hh has its own cache Sh(ℓ)S^{(\ell)}_{h} with |Sh(ℓ)|≤sh|S^{(\ell)}_{h}|\leq s_{h}, the query aggregates attention outputs across all heads, so the set of tokens that can influence it in one layer is the union ⋃hSh(ℓ)\bigcup_{h}S^{(\ell)}_{h}, of size at most ∑hsh\sum_{h}s_{h}. Redistributing a fixed total budget ∑hsh\sum_{h}s_{h} across heads does not alter the bounds; only the total capacity matters.

Definition 2.4 (kk-hop pointer chasing, PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k}).

Input: a permutation π:[n]→[n]\pi:[n]\to[n] (where [n]={1,2,…,n}[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}), encoded as nn input tokens at positions 1,…,n1,\dots,n (token at position ii holds the pair (i,π⁡(i))(i,\pi(i))), plus a query token at a separate position indexed 00 (so the total number of token positions is n+1n+1, indexed {0,1,…,n}\{0,1,\dots,n\}; the query position 00 is not in π\pi’s domain). The chain is defined by z0:=1z_{0}:=1 and zt+1:=π⁡(zt)z_{t+1}:=\pi(z_{t}) for t≥0t\geq 0, so zt∈[n]z_{t}\in[n] for all tt. Output: zk=πk​(1)z_{k}=\pi^{k}(1). Unless stated, we assume n≥4​kn\geq 4k.

3 Main Results

We state the four main theorems; proofs appear in Section 4.

3.1 Product lower bound (conjectured)

Conjecture 3.1 (Product depth lower bound).

There exist universal constants c>0c>0 and n0≥1n_{0}\geq 1 such that for all n≥n0n\geq n_{0}, any (L,H,m,p,s)(L,H,m,p,s)-Cache-Transformer with a locality-respecting cache controller (Definition 4.6) solving PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k} correctly on all inputs with n≥4​kn\geq 4k and s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 satisfies

L≥c⋅⌈ks⌉⋅⌈log2⁡nH​m​p⌉.L\;\geq\;c\cdot\left\lceil\frac{k}{s}\right\rceil\cdot\left\lceil\frac{\log_{2}n}{Hmp}\right\rceil. (1)

For s>n/4s>\sqrt{n}/4, we conjecture only the unconditional max-bound of Proposition 4.4; whether the product structure extends to this regime is open (see Open Problem 2 in Section 8). Note that in this regime, the cache-reachability factor from Proposition 4.4 is ⌈(k−1)/s⌉\lceil(k-1)/s\rceil rather than ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil, a unit-level difference; the strengthening to ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil in Lemma 4.16 uses the cycle-structure restriction and therefore applies only in the s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 regime.

We refer to this as Conjecture 3.1 throughout; all downstream corollaries that rely on the product bound are flagged explicitly as conditional on it.

Evidence for Conjecture 3.1.

We provide three independent pieces of partial evidence:

  1. 1.

    Matching upper bound within O⁡(H​log⁡s)O(H\log s) (Theorem 3.2): windowed pointer doubling achieves L=O⁡(⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡(2​s)⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)L=O(\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}(2s)\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil). The lower bound in Conjecture 3.1 matches this upper bound up to a multiplicative factor of O⁡(H​log⁡s)O(H\log s), which vanishes at s=O⁡(1)s=O(1) and H=1H=1.

  2. 2.

    Consistency with all known algorithms: every correct algorithm we have analyzed satisfies the conjectured bound—either via an exit-based argument (Section 4) or via an intrinsic cost argument (serial chain-tracking has L=Θ⁡(k​log⁡n/(m​p))≥⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉L=\Theta(k\log n/(mp))\geq\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil since s​H≥1sH\geq 1).

  3. 3.

    Partial unconditional lower bound: we prove in Section 4 the max-bound L≥max⁡(⌈k/s⌉,⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉)L\geq\max(\lceil k/s\rceil,\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil) unconditionally (Proposition 4.4), and the conjecture additionally holds unconditionally in the restricted subregime s⋅2m​p<8s\cdot 2^{mp}<8 under the stronger query-only controller assumption (Remark 4.13, “Partial progress” paragraph). The gap between the unconditional max-bound and the conjectured product-bound is exactly one multiplicative factor of ⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil or of ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil, whichever is smaller.

Closing Conjecture 3.1—either by direct proof or by disproof and replacement—is the central technical question left open by this work; we discuss it as Open Problem 1 in Section 8.

This conjectured bound is strictly stronger than the unconditional L≥max⁡(⌈k/s⌉,⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉)L\geq\max(\lceil k/s\rceil,\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil): cache and bandwidth bottlenecks would interact multiplicatively through the sequential dependency of the pointer chain, rather than competing. The locality restriction is essential for the bandwidth factor; without it, only the cache-reachability factor ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil can be proved (Lemma 4.1).

Theorem 3.2 (Matching upper bound).

For any n,k,sn,k,s with 1≤s≤n1\leq s\leq n, there exists a single-head (L,1,m,p,s)(L,1,m,p,s)-Cache-Transformer solving PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k} with

L=O⁡(min⁡(k,⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡(2​s)⌉)⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉).L\;=\;O\!\left(\min\bigl(k,\,\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}(2s)\rceil\bigr)\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil\right).

(We use ⌈log2⁡(2​s)⌉≥1\lceil\log_{2}(2s)\rceil\geq 1 to ensure the bound is non-vacuous at s=1s=1, where the min\min degenerates to the serial cost O⁡(k⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)O(k\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil).)

The two bounds combine to ks⋅log⁡nH​m​p≲L≲ks⋅log⁡s⋅log⁡nm​p\frac{k}{s}\cdot\frac{\log n}{Hmp}\lesssim L\lesssim\frac{k}{s}\cdot\log s\cdot\frac{\log n}{mp}, a multiplicative gap of O⁡(H​log⁡s)O(H\log s), which vanishes at s=O⁡(1)s=O(1) and H=1H=1.

Corollary 3.3 (Minimum cache formula, conditional on Conjecture 3.1).

Conditional on Conjecture 3.1 and in its regime (s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4, n≥4​kn\geq 4k), to achieve depth LL with a locality-respecting controller,

s=Ω⁡(max⁡(kL,k​log2​nL⋅H​m​p)).s\;=\;\Omega\!\left(\max\!\left(\frac{k}{L},\;\frac{k\log_{2}n}{L\cdot Hmp}\right)\right).

The first term (cache reachability) dominates when H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n; the second (bandwidth) dominates in narrow or low-precision models and is conditional on the product bound of Conjecture 3.1. Unconditionally (from Proposition 4.4), only the weaker s=Ω⁡(k/L)s=\Omega(k/L) is guaranteed.

Corollary 3.4 (Depth transition at critical cache size).

Define s⋆=n⁡⌈log2⁡k⌉/ks^{\star}=n\lceil\log_{2}k\rceil/k. Assume k→∞k\to\infty with k=o⁡(n/log⁡n)k=o(n/\log n) (which ensures both s⋆=ω⁡(log⁡k)s^{\star}=\omega(\log k) and s⋆=o⁡(n)s^{\star}=o(n), so s⋆s^{\star} is a non-trivial threshold in (log⁡k,n)(\log k,n)) and m​p=Ω⁡(log⁡n)mp=\Omega(\log n) (a realistic LLM precision regime). Then up to logarithmic factors:

  • •

    For s≥s⋆s\geq s^{\star}: windowed pointer doubling achieves L=O⁡((k/s)​log⁡s⋅log⁡n/(m​p))L=O((k/s)\log s\cdot\log n/(mp)), and the ratio (L/k)=O⁡((log⁡s​log⁡n)/(s⋅m​p))=o⁡(1)(L/k)=O((\log s\log n)/(s\cdot mp))=o(1) under the precision assumption, so L=o⁡(k)L=o(k).

  • •

    For s<s⋆s<s^{\star}: any correct algorithm requires L≥⌈k/s⌉L\geq\lceil k/s\rceil; the serial strategy achieves L=O⁡(k​log⁡n/(m​p))=O⁡(k)L=O(k\log n/(mp))=O(k).

Below s⋆s^{\star}, the upper-bound strategy we know (serial chain-tracking) incurs L=Θ⁡(k​log⁡n/(m​p))=Θ⁡(k)L=\Theta(k\log n/(mp))=\Theta(k), while the (unconditional) reachability lower bound L≥⌈k/s⌉L\geq\lceil k/s\rceil leaves a gap: the upper-bound parallelism advantage over RNNs disappears in the known algorithm, but the lower bound at s≫1s\gg 1 does not rule out faster parallel algorithms in principle. For s=O⁡(1)s=O(1) specifically, ⌈k/s⌉=Θ⁡(k)\lceil k/s\rceil=\Theta(k) matches the serial upper bound, giving a tight Θ⁡(k)\Theta(k) characterization in that sub-regime—comparable to RNNs (which are stuck at Θ⁡(k)\Theta(k) under (Sanford et al., 2024)’s conditional lower bound requiring RNN width O⁡(N/k6)O(N/k^{6})).

3.2 When the product bound binds: the bandwidth barrier

For standard LLM configurations (H=32H=32, m=128m=128, p=16p=16, so H​m​p≈6.5⋅104Hmp\approx 6.5\cdot 10^{4}), the bandwidth factor ⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil equals 11 for any realistic nn (up to n≤2H​m​p≫1019000n\leq 2^{Hmp}\gg 10^{19000}), and Conjecture 3.1 reduces to the cache-reachability bound L≥⌈k/s⌉L\geq\lceil k/s\rceil alone—a near-trivial consequence of the fact that the query token’s reachable set grows by at most ss per layer.

It is natural to ask whether the bandwidth factor can be strengthened. We show that, within a natural class of proof techniques, it cannot: any lower bound obtainable via per-window distinguishability counting saturates at ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil when H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n.

Definition 3.5 (Per-window distinguishability counting argument).

A lower-bound proof is a per-window distinguishability counting argument if it decomposes L≥W⋅BL\geq W\cdot B, where W=Ω⁡(⌈k/s⌉)W=\Omega(\lceil k/s\rceil) is a number of windows and BB is a per-window depth bound of the form

B≥⌈log2⁡MjH​m​p⌉,B\;\geq\;\left\lceil\frac{\log_{2}M_{j}}{Hmp}\right\rceil,

where MjM_{j} is a lower bound, at window jj, on the number of distinct per-window outputs zτjz_{\tau_{j}} that the algorithm must distinguish among inputs sharing a common pre-window query-state X0(ℓj−1)X^{(\ell_{j-1})}_{0}. This class includes the proof strategy for Conjecture 3.1, all reachability-plus-counting combinations, and finite-precision adaptations of (Sanford et al., 2024)’s technique.

Theorem 3.6 (Bandwidth barrier).

Let 𝒜\mathcal{A} be any per-window distinguishability counting argument (Definition 3.5) applied to PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k}. Then for each window jj, the per-window output count MjM_{j} satisfies Mj≤nM_{j}\leq n, so the bandwidth factor BB derived from 𝒜\mathcal{A} satisfies B≤⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉B\leq\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil. In particular, when H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n, B≤1B\leq 1, and 𝒜\mathcal{A} yields at most L≥W=O⁡(⌈k/s⌉)L\geq W=O(\lceil k/s\rceil), matching the cache-reachability bound.

Furthermore, the barrier is structural: any modification of PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k} that keeps per-window output within [n][n] inherits Mj≤nM_{j}\leq n and the same saturation.

Remark 3.7 (On the conceptual depth of the barrier).

In some sense, Theorem 3.6 is a direct consequence of the fact that the per-window output lies in [n][n], making it look tautological. However, its role is to formalize a class of proof techniques (Definition 3.5) and show that the entire class ceilings at ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil when H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n. This is analogous to formalizing “natural proofs” in circuit complexity: once the class is defined, the impossibility within that class is near-immediate, but the formalization itself identifies what bypass mechanisms are needed. Our “eight handles” analysis (Section 4.4) systematically confirms that no bypass we could identify escapes the class.

Proof.

The per-window output of PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k} is zτj=πτj​(1)∈[n]z_{\tau_{j}}=\pi^{\tau_{j}}(1)\in[n], which takes at most nn distinct values as π\pi varies (regardless of any conditioning). By the definition of MjM_{j} (Definition 3.5) as a lower bound on the support size of zτjz_{\tau_{j}} under some conditioning, we have Mj≤nM_{j}\leq n. The inequality B≤⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉B\leq\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil is then immediate, and equals 11 when H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n. The modification claim is immediate: any task with per-window output in a set of size ≤n\leq n gives Mj≤nM_{j}\leq n. ∎

We discuss in Section 8 what it would take to break this barrier: translating unconditional communication-complexity lower bounds for pointer chasing (Nisan and Wigderson, 1993; Yehudayoff, 2020; Mao et al., 2025) into Cache-Transformer depth lower bounds without the MPC conjecture (an open problem) or genuinely different proof techniques not of the form in Definition 3.5. The barrier is not a proof gap in our work; it is a structural obstacle on the current road to depth lower bounds in the standard LLM regime.

3.3 Error amplification under random cache selection

The empirical observation (Ananthanarayanan et al., 2026) that multi-hop accuracy drops precipitously under random cache selection can be partially explained by bounds on the joint success probability of windowed pointer doubling. We analyze this algorithm: at each of T=⌈log2⁡k⌉T=\lceil\log_{2}k\rceil stages, the algorithm needs to find a destination dt=πt​(1)d_{t}=\pi^{t}(1) (for simplicity of exposition we take a consecutive-destination chain; the pointer-doubling structure is analogous) in a cache Ct⊆[n]C_{t}\subseteq[n] of size ss. The algorithm succeeds at stage tt if dt∈Ctd_{t}\in C_{t}, and succeeds overall (event ℰ\mathcal{E}) if all TT stages succeed.

We establish three results: a tight exponential bound for oblivious caches, a tight stage-1-dominated bound for adaptive caches matched by an explicit construction, and a quantitative separation between the two.

Theorem 3.8 (Oblivious caches: exponential decay in TT).

Let π∼Unif⁡(Sn)\pi\sim\mathrm{Unif}(S_{n}) with n≥T+1n\geq T+1. For any oblivious cache selection (each CtC_{t} chosen without access to π\pi; the CtC_{t} may share common randomness),

Pr⁡[ℰ]≤(sn−T)T+2​T3n.\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\;\leq\;\left(\frac{s}{n-T}\right)^{T}\;+\;\frac{2T^{3}}{n}.

In the sub-regime where the main term dominates the error term—precisely when sT≥2​T3​nT−1s^{T}\geq 2T^{3}n^{T-1} (equivalently (s/n)T≥2​T3/n(s/n)^{T}\geq 2T^{3}/n)—the bound exhibits exponential decay in TT of rate (s/n)T(s/n)^{T}. Outside this sub-regime (e.g., s=o⁡(n)s=o(n) with T=ω⁡(1)T=\omega(1) and sTs^{T} growing slower than T3​nT−1T^{3}n^{T-1}) the error term 2​T3/n2T^{3}/n dominates and the bound degenerates to O⁡(T3/n)O(T^{3}/n).

Theorem 3.9 (Adaptive caches: tight Θ⁡(s/n)\Theta(s/n)).

Let π∼Unif⁡(Sn)\pi\sim\mathrm{Unif}(S_{n}) with n≥T+1n\geq T+1. For any locality-respecting adaptive cache controller (Definition 4.6),

Pr⁡[ℰ]≤sn.\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\;\leq\;\frac{s}{n}.

Moreover, this is tight: there is an explicit locality-respecting adaptive controller (“chain-tracking”) achieving Pr⁡[ℰ]≥s/n\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\geq s/n, matching the upper bound with exact equality.

Corollary 3.10 (Adaptive-oblivious separation).

In the regime sT≥2​T3​nT−1s^{T}\geq 2T^{3}n^{T-1} (equivalently, s≥(2​T3)1/T⋅n(T−1)/Ts\geq(2T^{3})^{1/T}\cdot n^{(T-1)/T}) and T≤n/2T\leq\sqrt{n}/2, in which the main term of Theorem 3.8 dominates the error term, the optimal adaptive success probability exceeds the best oblivious success probability by a factor of at least

Pr⁡[ℰ]adaptiveoptPr⁡[ℰ]obliviousopt≥Ω⁡((ns)T−1).\frac{\Pr[\mathcal{E}]_{\mathrm{adaptive}}^{\mathrm{opt}}}{\Pr[\mathcal{E}]_{\mathrm{oblivious}}^{\mathrm{opt}}}\;\geq\;\Omega\!\left(\left(\frac{n}{s}\right)^{T-1}\right).

Outside this regime, the separation is Ω⁡(s/T3)\Omega(s/T^{3}), still a non-trivial multiplicative gap.

Remark 3.11 (What this says about adaptive vs. oblivious eviction).

Theorems 3.8 and 3.9 together give a sharp answer to why adaptive (heavy-hitter, attention-score) eviction outperforms oblivious (recency, random) baselines in practice, as reported by Liu et al. (2025): the two regimes exhibit qualitatively different scaling behavior with chain length. Under uniform random cache selection—the worst case for the algorithm—oblivious caches see joint success probability decay as (s/n)T(s/n)^{T}, while adaptive caches see decay as only s/ns/n (no TT dependence). The adaptive controller exploits the structure that learning early chain values reveals later ones via locality. Our bound is non-asymptotic and parameter-free: it applies to any locality-respecting controller, and the achievability construction demonstrates the bound cannot be improved beyond constants.

Remark 3.12 (Relation to empirical observations).

At n=16,s=8,k=8n=16,s=8,k=8 (Figure 1c), empirical joint success under random (oblivious) cache is ≈17.5%\approx 17.5\%. The main term of Theorem 3.8 gives (s/(n−T))T=(8/13)3≈23.3%(s/(n-T))^{T}=(8/13)^{3}\approx 23.3\%, which consistently upper-bounds the good-chain success probability Pr⁡[ℰgood]\Pr[\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{good}}]; however, Theorem 3.8’s full bound (s/(n−T))T+2​T3/n≈361%(s/(n-T))^{T}+2T^{3}/n\approx 361\% is vacuous (exceeds 1) at this small nn due to the error term. We distinguish two senses of “non-vacuous”: (a) bound <1<1, requiring only 2​T3/n<12T^{3}/n<1, i.e., n>2​T3n>2T^{3} (n≥55n\geq 55 for T=3T=3); (b) main term dominates error term, i.e., (s/n)T>2​T3/n(s/n)^{T}>2T^{3}/n, equivalently sT/nT−1>2​T3s^{T}/n^{T-1}>2T^{3}, i.e., n<sT/(T−1)/(2​T3)1/(T−1)n<s^{T/(T-1)}/(2T^{3})^{1/(T-1)} [equivalently n>2​T3/(s/n)Tn>2T^{3}/(s/n)^{T} in the fixed-ratio parameterization]. For T=3T=3 and s/n=cs/n=c constant, this gives n>2​T3/cT=54/c3n>2T^{3}/c^{T}=54/c^{3}; e.g., c=1/2c=1/2 requires n>432n>432, while c≈1c\approx 1 (near-full cache) gives n≳54n\gtrsim 54. In sense (a) the theorem rules out 100% success; in sense (b) the theorem’s (s/n)T(s/n)^{T} decay rate is the informative feature. The main term alone empirically upper-bounds good-chain success for all n≥T+1n\geq T+1. Quantitative sharpness of the full bound requires moderate-to-large nn.

When the bandwidth factor binds quantitatively.

In the barrier regime (H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n), the product bound of Conjecture 3.1 would reduce to ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil and coincide with the cache-reachability bound. In the narrow-model regime (H​m​p<log2⁡nHmp<\log_{2}n: e.g., H=1H=1, m=4m=4, p=4p=4 giving H​m​p=16Hmp=16; or single-head INT4 with m=16m=16, p=4p=4, H=1H=1), the bandwidth factor is strictly greater than 11 and the conjectured product structure is quantitatively binding. This regime is increasingly relevant for quantized and edge-deployed models.

4 Proofs

4.1 Cache reachability

The first ingredient is a size bound on the set of input tokens on which the query-token representation can functionally depend. This set grows by at most ss per layer, reflecting the fact that the cache at each layer adds ss new indices to the query’s reachable support.

Lemma 4.1 (Reachability).

Define the functional-dependence set Dℓ​(0)​(π)⊆[N]D_{\ell}(0)(\pi)\subseteq[N] of the query token at layer ℓ\ell, for each input π\pi, as the minimal set of input tokens such that X0(ℓ)​(π)X^{(\ell)}_{0}(\pi) is a function of {xj​(π):j∈Dℓ​(0)​(π)}\{x_{j}(\pi):j\in D_{\ell}(0)(\pi)\} together with the (deterministic) weights and cache-selection rules. The set is defined pointwise in π\pi (not as a single fixed set covering all π\pi), which is the right notion for adaptive controllers where the reachable support varies with the input. Then

D0​(0)={0},Dℓ​(0)⊆Dℓ−1​(0)∪S(ℓ)∪⋃j∈S(ℓ)Dℓ−1​(j),D_{0}(0)=\{0\},\qquad D_{\ell}(0)\;\subseteq\;D_{\ell-1}(0)\cup S^{(\ell)}\cup\bigcup_{j\in S^{(\ell)}}D_{\ell-1}(j),

and in particular

|DL​(0)|≤ 1+L⋅s.|D_{L}(0)|\;\leq\;1+L\cdot s. (2)
Proof.

The first inclusion is immediate from the attention update rule: X0(ℓ)X^{(\ell)}_{0} is computed from X0(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{0} and the keys/values of tokens j∈S(ℓ)j\in S^{(\ell)}, which in turn are functions of Xj(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{j}. So X0(ℓ)X^{(\ell)}_{0} depends only on layer-(ℓ−1)(\ell-1) representations of tokens in {0}∪S(ℓ)\{0\}\cup S^{(\ell)}, each of which depends only on inputs in Dℓ−1​(j)D_{\ell-1}(j).

For the size bound (2), the naive induction on the recursion above does not work: ⋃j∈S(ℓ)Dℓ−1​(j)\bigcup_{j\in S^{(\ell)}}D_{\ell-1}(j) can be as large as |S(ℓ)|⋅maxj⁡|Dℓ−1​(j)||S^{(\ell)}|\cdot\max_{j}|D_{\ell-1}(j)|. Instead, we argue differently. For each layer ℓ′∈{1,…,L}\ell^{\prime}\in\{1,\dots,L\}, let Nℓ′=S(ℓ′)N_{\ell^{\prime}}=S^{(\ell^{\prime})} be the set of cache-accessible token indices at that layer. We claim

DL​(0)⊆{0}∪⋃ℓ′=1LNℓ′.D_{L}(0)\;\subseteq\;\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}=1}^{L}N_{\ell^{\prime}}. (3)

Given (3), the size bound follows immediately: |DL​(0)|≤1+∑ℓ′=1L|S(ℓ′)|≤1+L​s|D_{L}(0)|\leq 1+\sum_{\ell^{\prime}=1}^{L}|S^{(\ell^{\prime})}|\leq 1+Ls.

To prove (3), we show by induction on ℓ\ell that for every token i∈[N]i\in[N],

Dℓ​(i)⊆{i}∪⋃ℓ′=1ℓNℓ′.D_{\ell}(i)\;\subseteq\;\{i\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}=1}^{\ell}N_{\ell^{\prime}}. (4)

Base case ℓ=0\ell=0: D0​(i)={i}D_{0}(i)=\{i\}, trivially contained in the right-hand side. Inductive step: by the recursion, Dℓ​(i)⊆Dℓ−1​(i)∪S(ℓ)∪⋃j∈S(ℓ)Dℓ−1​(j)D_{\ell}(i)\subseteq D_{\ell-1}(i)\cup S^{(\ell)}\cup\bigcup_{j\in S^{(\ell)}}D_{\ell-1}(j). By the inductive hypothesis applied to ii and to each j∈S(ℓ)=Nℓj\in S^{(\ell)}=N_{\ell},

Dℓ−1​(i)⊆{i}∪⋃ℓ′=1ℓ−1Nℓ′,Dℓ−1​(j)⊆{j}∪⋃ℓ′=1ℓ−1Nℓ′.D_{\ell-1}(i)\subseteq\{i\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}=1}^{\ell-1}N_{\ell^{\prime}},\qquad D_{\ell-1}(j)\subseteq\{j\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}=1}^{\ell-1}N_{\ell^{\prime}}.

Taking the union with NℓN_{\ell} and using {j}⊆Nℓ\{j\}\subseteq N_{\ell} for j∈Nℓj\in N_{\ell}:

Dℓ​(i)⊆{i}∪Nℓ∪⋃ℓ′=1ℓ−1Nℓ′={i}∪⋃ℓ′=1ℓNℓ′.∎D_{\ell}(i)\subseteq\{i\}\cup N_{\ell}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}=1}^{\ell-1}N_{\ell^{\prime}}=\{i\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}=1}^{\ell}N_{\ell^{\prime}}.\qed

Observe that Lemma 4.1 does not depend on how the caches S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)} are chosen—adaptive or oblivious, data-dependent or not—because the cache sets enter the bound as sets of indices, and the union argument is index-based. This is crucial for the trace-equivalence argument (Lemma 4.10) below.

4.2 Bandwidth bound via counting

Lemma 4.2 (Distinguishability bound).

Fix any layer ℓ0\ell_{0} and any value x∈𝒬pmx\in\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m}. Over all inputs π\pi such that X0(ℓ0)​(π)=xX^{(\ell_{0})}_{0}(\pi)=x, and over all adaptive cache choices, the set

ΣB​(x):={X0(ℓ0+B)​(π):π​ such that ​X0(ℓ0)​(π)=x}\Sigma_{B}(x)\;:=\;\bigl\{X^{(\ell_{0}+B)}_{0}(\pi)\;:\;\pi\text{ such that }X^{(\ell_{0})}_{0}(\pi)=x\bigr\}

has cardinality at most 2B⋅H​m​p2^{B\cdot Hmp}.

Proof.

At each layer ℓ\ell, the query-token update takes the form

X0(ℓ)=ϕℓ​(X0(ℓ−1)+∑h=1Ha0(ℓ,h)​WO(ℓ,h)),X^{(\ell)}_{0}\;=\;\phi_{\ell}\!\left(X^{(\ell-1)}_{0}\;+\;\sum_{h=1}^{H}a^{(\ell,h)}_{0}\,W^{(\ell,h)}_{O}\right),

where ϕℓ\phi_{\ell} is the deterministic MLP+quantization map and a0(ℓ,h)∈𝒬pma^{(\ell,h)}_{0}\in\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m} is the quantized attention output of head hh. By Definition 2.1, every intermediate activation—including each a0(ℓ,h)a^{(\ell,h)}_{0}—is quantized to pp bits per coordinate before use, so |𝒬pm|≤2m​p|\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m}|\leq 2^{mp}. The softmax attention weights may themselves be computed in continuous arithmetic, but the attention output vectors a0(ℓ,h)a^{(\ell,h)}_{0} are rounded to 𝒬pm\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m} before being added via the residual connection; our bound applies to these outputs, not to the internal softmax computation.

Thus, given a fixed X0(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{0}, the next-layer value X0(ℓ)X^{(\ell)}_{0} is determined by the tuple (a0(ℓ,1),…,a0(ℓ,H))∈(𝒬pm)H(a^{(\ell,1)}_{0},\dots,a^{(\ell,H)}_{0})\in(\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m})^{H}, of which there are at most (2m​p)H=2H​m​p(2^{mp})^{H}=2^{Hmp}. Iterating from X0(ℓ0)=xX^{(\ell_{0})}_{0}=x for BB layers gives |ΣB​(x)|≤(2H​m​p)B=2B⋅H​m​p.|\Sigma_{B}(x)|\leq(2^{Hmp})^{B}=2^{B\cdot Hmp}. (Note that the trivial bound |ΣB​(x)|≤|𝒬pm|=2m​p|\Sigma_{B}(x)|\leq|\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m}|=2^{mp} also holds for all B≥1B\geq 1, since ΣB​(x)⊆𝒬pm\Sigma_{B}(x)\subseteq\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m}. The BB-dependent form 2B⋅H​m​p2^{B\cdot Hmp} is looser in absolute terms when B​H≥1BH\geq 1, but it is the form required downstream: we use this lemma to prove a lower bound on BB, so expressing the reachable-state count as growing with BB is essential—the trivial 2m​p2^{mp} bound is independent of BB and cannot force BB to be large.) ∎

Remark 4.3 (Why this avoids the softmax objection).

We make no claim about how softmax computes attention weights. Those weights can be continuous, data-dependent, and arbitrarily complex. Our bound applies to the output of attention—an mm-dimensional vector quantized to pp bits—not to the internal mechanism. This is a physical constraint: GPU hardware represents attention outputs in finite precision.

4.3 Sequential windows

Before presenting the full proof strategy, we record an unconditional lower bound that follows from Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2 alone (no invocation of Lemma 4.11 or Lemma 4.14):

Proposition 4.4 (Unconditional max-bound).

Any (L,H,m,p,s)(L,H,m,p,s)-Cache-Transformer solving PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k} correctly on all inputs with n≥4​kn\geq 4k satisfies

L≥max⁡(⌈k−1s⌉,⌈log2⁡nH​m​p⌉)≥max⁡(⌈k/s⌉−1,⌈log2⁡nH​m​p⌉).L\;\geq\;\max\!\left(\left\lceil\frac{k-1}{s}\right\rceil,\;\left\lceil\frac{\log_{2}n}{Hmp}\right\rceil\right)\;\geq\;\max\!\left(\lceil k/s\rceil-1,\;\left\lceil\frac{\log_{2}n}{Hmp}\right\rceil\right).
Proof.

Cache-reachability factor. Fix any π\pi with cycle of 11 of length >k>k (such π\pi exist for n≥k+1n\geq k+1), so that z0=1,z1,…,zkz_{0}=1,z_{1},\ldots,z_{k} are pairwise distinct. For the algorithm to output zk​(π)=π⁡(zk−1​(π))z_{k}(\pi)=\pi(z_{k-1}(\pi)) correctly, its final query-token state X0(L)X^{(L)}_{0} must depend on the value π⁡(zk−1)\pi(z_{k-1}). Iterating the same argument for zk−2,zk−3,…z_{k-2},z_{k-3},\ldots (since knowing zk−1=π⁡(zk−2)z_{k-1}=\pi(z_{k-2}) likewise requires zk−2∈TLz_{k-2}\in T_{L}, and so on), we obtain {z0,z1,…,zk−1}⊆TL​(π)\{z_{0},z_{1},\ldots,z_{k-1}\}\subseteq T_{L}(\pi). These kk positions are distinct, so |TL​(π)|≥k|T_{L}(\pi)|\geq k. Combined with Lemma 4.1’s upper bound |TL​(π)|≤1+L​s|T_{L}(\pi)|\leq 1+Ls, we get 1+L​s≥k1+Ls\geq k, i.e., L≥⌈(k−1)/s⌉L\geq\lceil(k-1)/s\rceil.

Output-bandwidth factor. A correct algorithm determines zkz_{k} from the final query-token state X0(L)X^{(L)}_{0}, so the map π↦X0(L)​(π)\pi\mapsto X^{(L)}_{0}(\pi) must take at least nn distinct values: for each target value v∈[n]v\in[n], there exists a permutation πv∈Sn\pi_{v}\in S_{n} with zk​(πv)=vz_{k}(\pi_{v})=v. For v=1v=1: take πv\pi_{v} with a cycle of length exactly kk on {1,a1,…,ak−1}\{1,a_{1},\ldots,a_{k-1}\} (for any distinct a1,…,ak−1∈[n]∖{1}a_{1},\ldots,a_{k-1}\in[n]\setminus\{1\}), i.e., πv​(1)=a1,πv​(ai)=ai+1\pi_{v}(1)=a_{1},\pi_{v}(a_{i})=a_{i+1} for i=1,…,k−2i=1,\ldots,k-2, and πv​(ak−1)=1\pi_{v}(a_{k-1})=1; then zi​(πv)=aiz_{i}(\pi_{v})=a_{i} for i=1,…,k−1i=1,\ldots,k-1 and zk​(πv)=1=vz_{k}(\pi_{v})=1=v. Distinct vv’s require distinct final states. By Lemma 4.2 applied from the fixed initial state X0(0)X^{(0)}_{0}, |ΣL​(X0(0))|≤2L⋅H​m​p|\Sigma_{L}(X^{(0)}_{0})|\leq 2^{L\cdot Hmp}, hence 2L​H​m​p≥n2^{LHmp}\geq n, i.e., L≥⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉L\geq\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil. ∎

Conjecture 3.1 would strengthen this max to a product. The proof strategy occupying the rest of this section (Lemmas 4.11–4.19) implements the exit-based argument outlined in Section 3; the probabilistic step (⋆)(\star) of Lemma 4.11 is left as Open Problem 1. The ⌈(k−1)/s⌉\lceil(k-1)/s\rceil cache-reachability factor of Proposition 4.4 is strengthened to ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil via the sequential-windows argument (Lemma 4.16); since ⌈(k−1)/s⌉≥⌈k/s⌉−1\lceil(k-1)/s\rceil\geq\lceil k/s\rceil-1, this is a unit-level refinement and does not affect asymptotics.

Definition 4.5.

Partition the chain into W=⌈k/s⌉W=\lceil k/s\rceil windows. Window j∈{1,…,W}j\in\{1,\dots,W\} covers chain positions z(j−1)​s,…,zmin⁡(j​s,k)z_{(j-1)s},\dots,z_{\min(js,k)}; its boundary output is zmin⁡(j​s,k)z_{\min(js,k)}. For brevity write τj:=min⁡(j​s,k)\tau_{j}:=\min(js,k), so window jj’s output is zτjz_{\tau_{j}}.

Handling adaptive cache: trace equivalence under a locality assumption

A subtle issue is that the cache controller CℓC_{\ell} is defined (Definition 2.1) as a deterministic function of all layer-(ℓ−1)(\ell-1) representations, not just those in Dℓ−1​(0)D_{\ell-1}(0). A maximally adversarial controller could in principle read representations of tokens it has not yet cached, and thereby leak information about out-of-cache tokens into its subsequent cache choices. We rule this out with a natural restriction:

Definition 4.6 (Locality-respecting controller).

A cache controller CℓC_{\ell} is locality-respecting if, for every π\pi, the set S(ℓ)​(π)S^{(\ell)}(\pi) depends only on the representations {Xj(ℓ−1)​(π):j∈Tℓ​(π)}\{X^{(\ell-1)}_{j}(\pi):j\in T_{\ell}(\pi)\}, where Tℓ​(π):={0}∪⋃ℓ′<ℓS(ℓ′)​(π)T_{\ell}(\pi):=\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}<\ell}S^{(\ell^{\prime})}(\pi) is the cache support up to layer ℓ−1\ell-1. (This recursive definition is well-defined, as shown in Proposition 4.8 below.)

Remark 4.7 (Relation to Definition 2.1).

Definition 2.1 (model) permits CℓC_{\ell} to depend on all NN representations at layer ℓ−1\ell-1; Definition 4.6 (locality) further restricts this to positions the algorithm has already touched. Our lower bounds (Proposition 4.4, Conjecture 3.1, Theorem 3.6) apply to the locality-respecting class (a strict subclass); our upper bound (Theorem 3.2) is realized by a locality-respecting algorithm and hence applies to both classes. For positions j∈Tℓ∖S(ℓ−1)j\in T_{\ell}\setminus S^{(\ell-1)}, the representation Xj(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{j} is carried forward from the last layer at which jj participated in attention (residually unchanged); these are the “ghost states” for evicted tokens, consistent with KV compression systems in practice.

Proposition 4.8 (Well-definedness of the recursion).

The recursive definition is well-defined: for each ℓ∈{0,1,…,L}\ell\in\{0,1,\dots,L\}, Tℓ​(π)T_{\ell}(\pi), S(ℓ)​(π)S^{(\ell)}(\pi), and all representations Xj(ℓ)​(π)X^{(\ell)}_{j}(\pi) are deterministic functions of π|Tℓ​(π)\pi|_{T_{\ell}(\pi)}.

Proof.

By strong induction on ℓ\ell. For ℓ=0\ell=0: T0​(π)={0}T_{0}(\pi)=\{0\} (constant, not a function of π\pi at all); Xj(0)​(π)=xj​(π)X^{(0)}_{j}(\pi)=x_{j}(\pi) is the identity embedding, depending on π\pi only at position jj, so Xj(0)X^{(0)}_{j} for j∈T0j\in T_{0} depends on π|T0\pi|_{T_{0}}.

For ℓ≥1\ell\geq 1: assume the proposition holds for all ℓ′<ℓ\ell^{\prime}<\ell. Then Tℓ−1​(π)={0}∪⋃ℓ′<ℓ−1S(ℓ′)​(π)T_{\ell-1}(\pi)=\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell^{\prime}<\ell-1}S^{(\ell^{\prime})}(\pi) is a function of π|Tℓ−2​(π)\pi|_{T_{\ell-2}(\pi)} by the inductive hypothesis applied to ℓ−1\ell-1, and S(ℓ−1)​(π)S^{(\ell-1)}(\pi) is a function of {Xj(ℓ−2)​(π):j∈Tℓ−1​(π)}\{X^{(\ell-2)}_{j}(\pi):j\in T_{\ell-1}(\pi)\} by locality. Hence Tℓ​(π)=Tℓ−1​(π)∪S(ℓ−1)​(π)T_{\ell}(\pi)=T_{\ell-1}(\pi)\cup S^{(\ell-1)}(\pi) is a function of π|Tℓ−1​(π)\pi|_{T_{\ell-1}(\pi)}.

Representations Xj(ℓ)X^{(\ell)}_{j} for j∈Tℓj\in T_{\ell} are computed by attention over S(ℓ)​(π)⊆Tℓ​(π)S^{(\ell)}(\pi)\subseteq T_{\ell}(\pi) (by definition of TℓT_{\ell}), using as keys/values the layer-(ℓ−1)(\ell-1) representations at positions in S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)}. By the inductive hypothesis, these representations are functions of π|Tℓ−1⊆π|Tℓ\pi|_{T_{\ell-1}}\subseteq\pi|_{T_{\ell}}, completing the induction. ∎

Under this restriction, the controller at layer ℓ\ell only examines representations of tokens it has already accessed at some earlier layer. This restriction is satisfied by essentially all KV-compression methods (H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM, PyramidKV, heavy-hitter variants), and is physically natural: reading representations outside the cache would require loading them, defeating the purpose of cache compression. We briefly discuss the fully adversarial case in Open Problem 3 in the Discussion section. The lower bounds below implicitly assume a locality-respecting controller; this is made explicit in Conjecture 3.1.

Definition 4.9 (Cache trace).

For a fixed algorithm and a fixed input π\pi, the cache trace is 𝒯⁡(π):=(S(1)​(π),…,S(L)​(π))\mathcal{T}(\pi):=(S^{(1)}(\pi),\dots,S^{(L)}(\pi)), and its support is T⁡(π):={0}∪⋃ℓ=1LS(ℓ)​(π)T(\pi):=\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{\ell=1}^{L}S^{(\ell)}(\pi). By Lemma 4.1, |T⁡(π)|≤1+L​s|T(\pi)|\leq 1+Ls.

Lemma 4.10 (Trace equivalence).

Fix any algorithm with a locality-respecting controller. Suppose π1,π2\pi_{1},\pi_{2} satisfy π1|T⁡(π1)=π2|T⁡(π1)\pi_{1}|_{T(\pi_{1})}=\pi_{2}|_{T(\pi_{1})}. Then 𝒯⁡(π1)=𝒯⁡(π2)\mathcal{T}(\pi_{1})=\mathcal{T}(\pi_{2}), T⁡(π1)=T⁡(π2)T(\pi_{1})=T(\pi_{2}), and Xj(ℓ)​(π1)=Xj(ℓ)​(π2)X^{(\ell)}_{j}(\pi_{1})=X^{(\ell)}_{j}(\pi_{2}) for all ℓ∈{0,…,L}\ell\in\{0,\dots,L\} and j∈T⁡(π1)j\in T(\pi_{1}). In particular, X0(L)​(π1)=X0(L)​(π2)X^{(L)}_{0}(\pi_{1})=X^{(L)}_{0}(\pi_{2}).

Proof.

Write T1:=T⁡(π1)T_{1}:=T(\pi_{1}). We prove by induction on ℓ∈{0,1,…,L}\ell\in\{0,1,\dots,L\} the joint claim

(Hℓ): S(ℓ′)​(π2)=S(ℓ′)​(π1)S^{(\ell^{\prime})}(\pi_{2})=S^{(\ell^{\prime})}(\pi_{1}) for all ℓ′≤ℓ\ell^{\prime}\leq\ell, and Xj(ℓ′)​(π2)=Xj(ℓ′)​(π1)X^{(\ell^{\prime})}_{j}(\pi_{2})=X^{(\ell^{\prime})}_{j}(\pi_{1}) for all ℓ′≤ℓ\ell^{\prime}\leq\ell and j∈T1j\in T_{1}.

Base case ℓ=0\ell=0. The representation claim holds by hypothesis and because Xj(0)X^{(0)}_{j} is a fixed function of xjx_{j}. The cache claim is vacuous at ℓ′=0\ell^{\prime}=0.

Inductive step ℓ−1⇒ℓ\ell-1\Rightarrow\ell. Assume (Hℓ-1).

Step 1: Cache selection matches. By locality, S(ℓ)​(π)S^{(\ell)}(\pi) depends only on {Xj(ℓ−1)​(π):j∈Tℓ​(π)}\{X^{(\ell-1)}_{j}(\pi):j\in T_{\ell}(\pi)\}. By (Hℓ-1), S(ℓ′)​(π2)=S(ℓ′)​(π1)S^{(\ell^{\prime})}(\pi_{2})=S^{(\ell^{\prime})}(\pi_{1}) for ℓ′<ℓ\ell^{\prime}<\ell, so Tℓ​(π2)=Tℓ​(π1)=:Tℓ⋆⊆T1T_{\ell}(\pi_{2})=T_{\ell}(\pi_{1})=:T_{\ell}^{\star}\subseteq T_{1}. By (Hℓ-1), Xj(ℓ−1)​(π2)=Xj(ℓ−1)​(π1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{j}(\pi_{2})=X^{(\ell-1)}_{j}(\pi_{1}) for j∈Tℓ⋆j\in T_{\ell}^{\star}. So the controller’s input tuple is identical under π1\pi_{1} and π2\pi_{2}, hence S(ℓ)​(π2)=S(ℓ)​(π1)S^{(\ell)}(\pi_{2})=S^{(\ell)}(\pi_{1}).

Step 2: Representations on T1T_{1} match. With S(ℓ)​(π1)=S(ℓ)​(π2)=:S(ℓ)⊆T1S^{(\ell)}(\pi_{1})=S^{(\ell)}(\pi_{2})=:S^{(\ell)}\subseteq T_{1}, for any j∈T1j\in T_{1} the update

Xj(ℓ)​(π)=fℓ​(Xj(ℓ−1)​(π),{(Xi(ℓ−1)​(π),Ki​(π),Vi​(π)):i∈S(ℓ)})X^{(\ell)}_{j}(\pi)=f_{\ell}\bigl(X^{(\ell-1)}_{j}(\pi),\,\{(X^{(\ell-1)}_{i}(\pi),K_{i}(\pi),V_{i}(\pi)):i\in S^{(\ell)}\}\bigr)

receives inputs Xj(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{j} (with j∈T1j\in T_{1}, equal by (Hℓ-1)) and Xi(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{i} for i∈S(ℓ)⊆T1i\in S^{(\ell)}\subseteq T_{1} (also equal). Hence Xj(ℓ)​(π2)=Xj(ℓ)​(π1)X^{(\ell)}_{j}(\pi_{2})=X^{(\ell)}_{j}(\pi_{1}).

This closes the induction. Since 0∈T10\in T_{1}, X0(L)​(π1)=X0(L)​(π2)X^{(L)}_{0}(\pi_{1})=X^{(L)}_{0}(\pi_{2}). ∎

The locality assumption is exactly what lets Step 1 close: under a general controller, reading Xj(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{j} for some j∉T1j\notin T_{1} could distinguish π1\pi_{1} from π2\pi_{2} and cause S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)} to diverge.

Lemma 4.11 (Existence of a chain-exiting permutation).

Fix any algorithm with a locality-respecting controller. Suppose L≤n/(8​s)L\leq n/(8s), n≥4​kn\geq 4k, and τj≥2\tau_{j}\geq 2 (which excludes only the corner case τj=1\tau_{j}=1, i.e., j=1j=1 together with min⁡(s,k)=1\min(s,k)=1). Then there exists a permutation π1\pi_{1} and an index t⋆∈(τj−1,τj]t^{\star}\in(\tau_{j-1},\tau_{j}] such that zt⋆−1​(π1)∉T1:=T⁡(π1)z_{t^{\star}-1}(\pi_{1})\notin T_{1}:=T(\pi_{1}).

Proof sketch of Lemma 4.11.

By Lemma 4.1 and the hypothesis L≤n/(8​s)L\leq n/(8s), |T⁡(π)|≤1+L​s≤n/4|T(\pi)|\leq 1+Ls\leq n/4 for every π\pi, whenever n≥8n\geq 8. We sketch a probabilistic argument; see Remark 4.13 for a discussion of the remaining technical step.

Under the assumption τj≥2\tau_{j}\geq 2, let σj:=τj−1≥1\sigma_{j}:=\tau_{j}-1\geq 1 (we use σj\sigma_{j} throughout this proof and Remark 4.13 to avoid confusion with the window-boundary index τj−1\tau_{j-1}, which in general differs from τj−1\tau_{j}-1 when s≥2s\geq 2). So zσjz_{\sigma_{j}} is well-defined and, by distinctness (below), is not the fixed starting position z0=1z_{0}=1 (which is always in TT for a correct algorithm; see the proof of Lemma 4.14, Part (c)). Average over π∼Unif⁡(Sn)\pi\sim\mathrm{Unif}(S_{n}) and consider Pr[zσj(π)∈T(π)]\Pr[z_{\sigma_{j}}(\pi)\in T(\pi)]. Two facts:

  • •

    Distinctness. Let 𝒟chain\mathcal{D}_{\text{chain}} be the event that z0,…,zkz_{0},\dots,z_{k} are pairwise distinct, equivalently, the cycle of π\pi containing 11 has length >k>k. For π∼Unif⁡(Sn)\pi\sim\mathrm{Unif}(S_{n}), the cycle length of 11 is uniform on {1,…,n}\{1,\dots,n\}, so Pr⁡[𝒟chain]=1−k/n≥3/4\Pr[\mathcal{D}_{\text{chain}}]=1-k/n\geq 3/4.

  • •

    Marginal of endpoint. Conditional on 𝒟chain\mathcal{D}_{\text{chain}} and on σj≥1\sigma_{j}\geq 1, by symmetry within the cycle, zσj​(π)z_{\sigma_{j}}(\pi) is uniform on [n]∖{1}[n]\setminus\{1\}.

The desired conclusion Pr[zσj∈T]<1\Pr[z_{\sigma_{j}}\in T]<1 would follow from:

(⋆)Pr⁡[zσj​(π)∈T⁡(π)∣𝒟chain]≤𝔼⁡[|T⁡(π)|]n−1≤n/4n−1< 1/3,\text{($\star$)}\qquad\Pr[z_{\sigma_{j}}(\pi)\in T(\pi)\mid\mathcal{D}_{\text{chain}}]\;\leq\;\frac{\mathbb{E}[|T(\pi)|]}{n-1}\;\leq\;\frac{n/4}{n-1}\;<\;1/3,

giving Pr[zσj∈T]≤1/3+1/4=7/12<1\Pr[z_{\sigma_{j}}\in T]\leq 1/3+1/4=7/12<1. Existence of some π1\pi_{1} with zσj​(π1)∉T⁡(π1)z_{\sigma_{j}}(\pi_{1})\notin T(\pi_{1}) then follows, and taking t⋆≤τjt^{\star}\leq\tau_{j} to be the first chain position outside T⁡(π1)T(\pi_{1}) proves the lemma. ∎

Remark 4.12 (Corner case τj=1\tau_{j}=1).

When τj=1\tau_{j}=1—that is, j=1j=1 together with min⁡(s,k)=1\min(s,k)=1 (so either s=1s=1 or k=1k=1)—Lemma 4.11 is vacuously false: the only candidate t⋆=1t^{\star}=1 requires z0=1∉T⁡(π)z_{0}=1\notin T(\pi), which fails for any correct algorithm because 1∈TL1\in T_{L} is forced by reading π⁡(1)\pi(1) (proof of Lemma 4.14, Part (c)). However, this does not affect the proof strategy for Conjecture 3.1: we can directly establish a per-window cost ℓ1−ℓ0≥B−1\ell_{1}-\ell_{0}\geq B-1 for window 1 (with ℓ0:=0\ell_{0}:=0) via the bandwidth argument alone. Using the definition of ℓj\ell_{j} given in the proof strategy below (ℓj\ell_{j} is the earliest layer at which |Tℓ|≥τj|T_{\ell}|\geq\tau_{j}, see Section 4.3), window 1’s cache support must grow to |Tℓ1|≥1=τ1|T_{\ell_{1}}|\geq 1=\tau_{1}, which holds already at ℓ1=0\ell_{1}=0 since T0={0}T_{0}=\{0\} has size 11; but to additionally determine z1=π⁡(1)∈[n]z_{1}=\pi(1)\in[n] requires, by Lemma 4.2 applied from X0(0)X^{(0)}_{0}, that X0(ℓ1⋆)X^{(\ell^{\star}_{1})}_{0} at some layer ℓ1⋆≤L\ell^{\star}_{1}\leq L takes at least nn distinct values, giving ℓ1⋆≥⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉=B\ell^{\star}_{1}\geq\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil=B. Such ℓ1⋆\ell^{\star}_{1} exists and satisfies ℓ1⋆≤L\ell^{\star}_{1}\leq L: the final state X0(L)X^{(L)}_{0} must determine zkz_{k}, and for k≥1k\geq 1 distinguishing any two π,π′\pi,\pi^{\prime} with zk​(π)≠zk​(π′)z_{k}(\pi)\neq z_{k}(\pi^{\prime}) requires X0(L)​(π)≠X0(L)​(π′)X^{(L)}_{0}(\pi)\neq X^{(L)}_{0}(\pi^{\prime}), so X0(L)X^{(L)}_{0} takes at least nn distinct values (all nn outputs are realized; see Proposition 4.4’s output-bandwidth argument for the explicit construction). Hence L≥ℓ1⋆≥BL\geq\ell^{\star}_{1}\geq B. For k=1k=1: W=1W=1 and this already establishes the product bound L≥B=⌈k/s⌉⋅BL\geq B=\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot B (trivially, since ⌈1/s⌉=1\lceil 1/s\rceil=1). For s=1,k≥2s=1,k\geq 2: combine with the j≥2j\geq 2 windows handled by Lemma 4.11 to obtain the full W⋅BW\cdot B product bound.

Remark 4.13 (A technical gap in Lemma 4.11).

The proof sketch above reduces Lemma 4.11 to inequality (⋆)(\star). Establishing (⋆)(\star) requires controlling the joint distribution of (T​(π),zσj​(π))(T(\pi),z_{\sigma_{j}}(\pi)) conditional on 𝒟chain\mathcal{D}_{\text{chain}}, where σj:=τj−1\sigma_{j}:=\tau_{j}-1. Both quantities are π\pi-measurable, and for an adaptive, label-sensitive algorithm they are not independent in general: the algorithm’s cache trajectory could in principle correlate with specific chain values. A naive union bound yields only Pr⁡[zσj∈T|𝒟]≤𝔼⁡[|T|]/Pr⁡[𝒟]≤n/3\Pr[z_{\sigma_{j}}\in T|\mathcal{D}]\leq\mathbb{E}[|T|]/\Pr[\mathcal{D}]\leq n/3, which is too weak; tightening to (⋆)(\star) appears to require either a second-moment argument specific to the input distribution or a Yao-principle reduction against an explicit adversary.

Status of Conjecture 3.1. Lemmas 4.1, 4.2, 4.14, 4.16, 4.19 are proved without hidden probabilistic assumptions. Lemma 4.17 (Window incompressibility) depends on Lemma 4.11 (it invokes the existence of a window-jj exit) and therefore inherits the gap. The proof strategy of Section 4.3 is therefore complete modulo (⋆)(\star): establishing (⋆)(\star)—either by proving it for the uniform distribution or by exhibiting an adversarial family on which the conclusion of Lemma 4.11 holds directly—would turn Conjecture 3.1 into a theorem. Closing the gap is stated as Open Problem 1 in Section 8.

Partial progress: unconditional cache-coverage bound in a restricted parameter subregime, under a stronger controller assumption. We can establish Lemma 4.11 unconditionally under (i) the additional parameter hypothesis s⋅2m​p<8s\cdot 2^{mp}<8 (equivalent to m​p<3−log2⁡smp<3-\log_{2}s) and (ii) the stronger controller assumption that CℓC_{\ell} is a deterministic function of the query-token state X0(ℓ−1)X^{(\ell-1)}_{0} alone (rather than of all {Xj(ℓ−1):j∈Tℓ}\{X^{(\ell-1)}_{j}:j\in T_{\ell}\} as in Definition 4.6). This query-only controller class is strictly narrower than locality-respecting but still includes all known KV-compression heuristics that dispatch cache selection from a single “read-head” computation. Under (ii), the cache at each layer CℓC_{\ell} takes at most 2m​p2^{mp} distinct values across possible query states, yielding at most s⋅2m​ps\cdot 2^{mp} distinct (state, slot) pairs, hence at most s⋅2m​ps\cdot 2^{mp} distinct positions in [n][n] that can ever appear in the cache at layer ℓ\ell across different π\pi. Summed over ℓ\ell layers: at most ℓ⋅s⋅2m​p\ell\cdot s\cdot 2^{mp} distinct (layer, position) pairs. For chain-in-trace (zt​(π)∈T​(π)z_{t}(\pi)\in T(\pi) for all π∈𝒟\pi\in\mathcal{D} and all t≤τj−1t\leq\tau_{j}-1), every chain value zt​(π)z_{t}(\pi) for every π\pi must be a (layer, position) pair reached. Over π\pi, ztz_{t} takes ∼n\sim n distinct values, so we need ℓ⋅s⋅2m​p≥n−1\ell\cdot s\cdot 2^{mp}\geq n-1, i.e., ℓ≥(n−1)/(s⋅2m​p)\ell\geq(n-1)/(s\cdot 2^{mp}). Combined with the hypothesis L≤n/(8​s)L\leq n/(8s) of Lemma 4.11: under (i) s⋅2m​p<8s\cdot 2^{mp}<8, we get ℓ≥(n−1)/(s⋅2m​p)>(n−1)/8>n/(8​s)≥L\ell\geq(n-1)/(s\cdot 2^{mp})>(n-1)/8>n/(8s)\geq L for s≥1s\geq 1 and n≥2n\geq 2, contradicting ℓ≤L\ell\leq L—so exit exists. The subregime s⋅2m​p<8s\cdot 2^{mp}<8 is restrictive; it captures only very low-precision scenarios (e.g., p=1,m=3,s=1p=1,m=3,s=1, giving m​p=3mp=3). This counting argument does not extend to moderate m​pmp (the cumulative cache coverage L⋅s⋅2m​pL\cdot s\cdot 2^{mp} grows beyond nn, permitting chain-in-trace without contradicting the layer budget), and it does not directly extend to general locality-respecting controllers (where CℓC_{\ell} can depend on all representations at positions in TℓT_{\ell}, so the cache-choice space is 2m​p​|Tℓ|2^{mp|T_{\ell}|} rather than 2m​p2^{mp}).

We flag this gap explicitly here, rather than obscure it, to give the reader an accurate picture of which parts of the argument are rigorous and which depend on a yet-unverified probabilistic step.

Lemma 4.14 (Adversarial permutation with preserved trace).

Fix any algorithm with a locality-respecting controller. Fix a reference π1\pi_{1} and exit index t⋆∈(τj−1,τj]t^{\star}\in(\tau_{j-1},\tau_{j}] with u:=zt⋆−1​(π1)∉T1:=T⁡(π1)u:=z_{t^{\star}-1}(\pi_{1})\notin T_{1}:=T(\pi_{1}), as provided by Lemma 4.11. Define the target set

𝒟:=[n]∖(T1∪{z0,…,zk}​(π1)∪π1​(T1)),\mathcal{D}\;:=\;[n]\setminus\bigl(T_{1}\cup\{z_{0},\dots,z_{k}\}(\pi_{1})\cup\pi_{1}(T_{1})\bigr),

of size |𝒟|≥n−2​(1+L​s)−(k+1)|\mathcal{D}|\geq n-2(1+Ls)-(k+1). For each d∈𝒟d\in\mathcal{D}, there is a permutation πd\pi_{d} such that:

  1. (a)

    πd|T1=π1|T1\pi_{d}|_{T_{1}}=\pi_{1}|_{T_{1}};

  2. (b)

    by (a) and Lemma 4.10, 𝒯⁡(πd)=𝒯⁡(π1)\mathcal{T}(\pi_{d})=\mathcal{T}(\pi_{1}), T⁡(πd)=T1T(\pi_{d})=T_{1}, and X0(ℓ)​(πd)=X0(ℓ)​(π1)X^{(\ell)}_{0}(\pi_{d})=X^{(\ell)}_{0}(\pi_{1}) for all ℓ\ell;

  3. (c)

    zt⋆​(πd)=dz_{t^{\star}}(\pi_{d})=d, and distinct d,d′∈𝒟d,d^{\prime}\in\mathcal{D} yield distinct zt⋆z_{t^{\star}} (since zt⋆​(πd)=dz_{t^{\star}}(\pi_{d})=d).

Proof.

Construction of πd\pi_{d}. For d∈𝒟d\in\mathcal{D}, observe π1−1​(d)∉T1\pi_{1}^{-1}(d)\notin T_{1}: if π1−1​(d)∈T1\pi_{1}^{-1}(d)\in T_{1}, then d∈π1​(T1)d\in\pi_{1}(T_{1}), contradicting d∉π1​(T1)d\notin\pi_{1}(T_{1}). Define

πd​(u):=d,πd​(π1−1​(d)):=π1​(u),πd​(x):=π1​(x)​ for all ​x∉{u,π1−1​(d)}.\pi_{d}(u):=d,\qquad\pi_{d}(\pi_{1}^{-1}(d)):=\pi_{1}(u),\qquad\pi_{d}(x):=\pi_{1}(x)\text{ for all }x\notin\{u,\pi_{1}^{-1}(d)\}.

This is a value-swap (transposition in the codomain) of π1\pi_{1}, hence a permutation. Both modified positions lie in [n]∖T1[n]\setminus T_{1}, so πd|T1=π1|T1\pi_{d}|_{T_{1}}=\pi_{1}|_{T_{1}}, giving (a). Part (b) follows from (a) by Lemma 4.10.

Part (c). We track the chain of πd\pi_{d} up to step t⋆t^{\star}. By Lemma 4.11, there exists an exit step in window jj, so (taking π1\pi_{1} to realize this) the π1\pi_{1}-orbit of z0=1z_{0}=1 has length at least t⋆t^{\star}, i.e., z0,z1,…,zt⋆−1z_{0},z_{1},\dots,z_{t^{\star}-1} are pairwise distinct under π1\pi_{1}. The chain up to zt⋆−1z_{t^{\star}-1} is the same under πd\pi_{d} as under π1\pi_{1}: this uses that πd\pi_{d} agrees with π1\pi_{1} on positions z0,z1,…,zt⋆−2z_{0},z_{1},\dots,z_{t^{\star}-2}. Remark 4.15 (Stopping at t⋆t^{\star} vs. reaching τj\tau_{j}).

Lemma 4.14 gives distinctness of zt⋆z_{t^{\star}}, not directly zτjz_{\tau_{j}}. When t⋆=τjt^{\star}=\tau_{j}, this is what we want. When t⋆<τjt^{\star}<\tau_{j}, the chain continues from dd for τj−t⋆\tau_{j}-t^{\star} more steps before reaching zτjz_{\tau_{j}}, and a priori two different d,d′∈𝒟d,d^{\prime}\in\mathcal{D} could produce the same zτjz_{\tau_{j}} through a chain collision (e.g., if dd lies in a 22-cycle of π1\pi_{1}).

We avoid this in two steps, both developed in the proof of Lemma 4.17:

  1. (i)

    Fix the first-exit step t0⋆t^{\star}_{0} by pigeonhole. The set 𝒩\mathcal{N} of permutations with a window-jj exit partitions by first-exit step into 𝒩=⨆t∈(τj−1,τj]𝒩t\mathcal{N}=\bigsqcup_{t\in(\tau_{j-1},\tau_{j}]}\mathcal{N}_{t} (at most ss parts). By pigeonhole at least one 𝒩t0⋆\mathcal{N}_{t^{\star}_{0}} has density ≥1/s\geq 1/s within 𝒩\mathcal{N}. Restrict to π1∈𝒩t0⋆\pi_{1}\in\mathcal{N}_{t^{\star}_{0}}.

  2. (ii)

    Restrict further to π1\pi_{1} with no short non-principal cycles. For s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4, permutations with all non-principal cycles of length >s>s form a positive-density subset of the conditioned ensemble.

Both restrictions reduce the set of valid reference permutations we may choose, but once a single valid π1\pi_{1} is fixed, the clean-target counting of Lemma 4.17 gives distinct zτjz_{\tau_{j}} values across the entire clean set of targets—no 1/s1/s loss propagates to the distinct-value count. The O⁡(H​log⁡s)O(H\log s) gap between Conjecture 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 is thus attributable entirely to the upper bound’s log2⁡(2​s)\log_{2}(2s) factor (from windowed doubling’s inner loop), not to the lower-bound proof.

Assume n≥4​kn\geq 4k and s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4. Suppose the algorithm, at layer ℓj\ell_{j}, produces a representation X0(ℓj)X^{(\ell_{j})}_{0} that determines zτjz_{\tau_{j}}. Lemma 4.16 is only a statement about the earliest layer at which window jj’s output can appear. To get the lower bound on total depth, we also need to control the number of layers that window jj consumes after window j−1j-1’s output has been resolved. This is the content of Lemma 4.17 and Lemma 4.19 below.

Lemma 4.17 (Window incompressibility).

Assume n≥4​kn\geq 4k and that the cache controller is locality-respecting (Definition 4.6). For any window index j∈{1,…,W}j\in\{1,\dots,W\}, there exist a layer ℓ†≤L\ell^{\dagger}\leq L and a value x†∈𝒬pmx^{\dagger}\in\mathcal{Q}_{p}^{m} such that, letting Π†:={π:X0(ℓ†)​(π)=x†}\Pi^{\dagger}:=\{\pi:X^{(\ell^{\dagger})}_{0}(\pi)=x^{\dagger}\}:

We do not assume t0⋆=τjt^{\star}_{0}=\tau_{j}.

Set ℓ†\ell^{\dagger} per cases (i)/(ii) and x†:=X0(ℓ†)​(π1)x^{\dagger}:=X^{(\ell^{\dagger})}_{0}(\pi_{1}) (in case (i), x†x^{\dagger} is the constant initial state, automatically).

Apply Lemma 4.14 to this π1\pi_{1} with exit index t⋆=t0⋆t^{\star}=t^{\star}_{0}. It produces a target set 𝒟\mathcal{D} of size ≥n−2​(1+L​s)−(k+1)≥n/2−k−O⁡(1)\geq n-2(1+Ls)-(k+1)\geq n/2-k-O(1). When t0⋆<τjt^{\star}_{0}<\tau_{j}, distinct zt0⋆z_{t^{\star}_{0}} values could in principle produce coinciding zτjz_{\tau_{j}} via chain collision after the exit step. We now count collision-inducing targets under the hypothesis s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4.

For d∈𝒟d\in\mathcal{D}: Lemma 4.14 constructs πd\pi_{d} by swapping values of π1\pi_{1} at u:=zt0⋆−1​(π1)u:=z_{t^{\star}_{0}-1}(\pi_{1}) and wd:=π1−1​(d)w_{d}:=\pi_{1}^{-1}(d) only. The chain of πd\pi_{d} starting from d=zt0⋆​(πd)d=z_{t^{\star}_{0}}(\pi_{d}) follows π1\pi_{1}’s iterations from dd until it hits one of the two swapped positions. We bound |𝒟∖clean||\mathcal{D}\setminus\text{clean}| by two contributions:

    Orbit hits uu: π1r​(d)=u\pi_{1}^{r}(d)=u for some r∈[0,Δ−1]r\in[0,\Delta-1], i.e., d∈{π1−r​(u):r∈[0,Δ−1]}d\in\{\pi_{1}^{-r}(u):r\in[0,\Delta-1]\}, at most Δ≤s\Delta\leq s values.

  2. (ii)

    Orbit hits wd=π1−1​(d)w_{d}=\pi_{1}^{-1}(d): π1r​(d)=π1−1​(d)\pi_{1}^{r}(d)=\pi_{1}^{-1}(d) for some r∈[0,Δ−1]r\in[0,\Delta-1], i.e., π1r+1​(d)=d\pi_{1}^{r+1}(d)=d, i.e., dd lies in a π1\pi_{1}-cycle of length dividing r+1∈[1,Δ]r+1\in[1,\Delta]. The number of such d∈[n]d\in[n] is at most ∑ℓ​ divides some ​r+1∈[1,Δ]ℓ⋅cℓ​(π1)≤∑ℓ≤Δℓ⋅cℓ​(π1)≤Δ⋅n≤s​n\sum_{\ell\text{ divides some }r+1\in[1,\Delta]}\ell\cdot c_{\ell}(\pi_{1})\leq\sum_{\ell\leq\Delta}\ell\cdot c_{\ell}(\pi_{1})\leq\Delta\cdot n\leq sn in worst case, where cℓ​(π1)c_{\ell}(\pi_{1}) is the number of π1\pi_{1}-cycles of length ℓ\ell. This worst-case bound is too weak.

To control (ii), we restrict attention to reference permutations π1\pi_{1} whose non-principal cycles all have length >s>s. For uniform π1∈Sn\pi_{1}\in S_{n} conditioned on 𝒟chain\mathcal{D}_{\text{chain}} (cycle of 11 has length >k>k), the probability of having no non-principal cycle of length ≤s\leq s is a positive density ρs>0\rho_{s}>0 (not uniform in ss: ρs\rho_{s} decreases as ss grows, but positivity for each fixed s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 is what we need). By classical cycle-structure asymptotics (e.g., Arratia–Tavaré), the number of cycles of each length ℓ\ell is approximately Poisson with mean 1/ℓ1/\ell for ℓ≤n1/2\ell\leq n^{1/2}, so the probability of having zero non-principal cycles of length ≤s\leq s satisfies ρs≈∏ℓ=1se−1/ℓ≥(es)−1\rho_{s}\approx\prod_{\ell=1}^{s}e^{-1/\ell}\geq(es)^{-1} for s=o⁡(n)s=o(\sqrt{n}) (valid under our precondition s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4). Thus a valid reference permutation π1\pi_{1} (one satisfying both the exit condition of Lemma 4.11 and the cycle-structure restriction) exists so long as the first-exit-step pigeonhole density 1/s1/s combined with ρs≥(e​s)−1\rho_{s}\geq(es)^{-1} gives positive probability; this holds throughout the precondition regime. Once a valid π1\pi_{1} is fixed, neither the first-exit-step pigeonhole nor the cycle-structure restriction propagates into the distinct-value count of zτjz_{\tau_{j}} (see final paragraph of proof and Remark 4.15).

Under this restriction, contribution (ii) vanishes (no short non-principal cycles), so |𝒟∖clean|≤s|\mathcal{D}\setminus\text{clean}|\leq s. Hence |clean|≥|𝒟|−s≥n/2−k−s|\text{clean}|\geq|\mathcal{D}|-s\geq n/2-k-s, and the injective map d↦π1Δ​(d)d\mapsto\pi_{1}^{\Delta}(d) on clean dd gives ≥n/2−k−s\geq n/2-k-s distinct values of zτj​(πd)z_{\tau_{j}}(\pi_{d}) on Π†\Pi^{\dagger}. Note: the first-exit-step pigeonhole and cycle-structure restriction only reduce the number of valid reference permutations π1\pi_{1}; once a single valid π1\pi_{1} is fixed, the distinct-value count of zτjz_{\tau_{j}} over the resulting {πd:d∈clean}⊆Π†\{\pi_{d}:d\in\text{clean}\}\subseteq\Pi^{\dagger} is ||clean|| directly, with no 1/s1/s factor. Thus the distinct-value count is ≥n/2−k−s≥n/4\geq n/2-k-s\geq n/4 in the regime s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 and n≥4​kn\geq 4k for nn sufficiently large.

For s>n/4s>\sqrt{n}/4, the cycle-restriction argument degrades and the product bound is not guaranteed by this proof strategy; we fall back to Proposition 4.4, consistent with the regime condition of Conjecture 3.1. ∎

Remark 4.18 (Effect on Conjecture 3.1’s constant).

The distinct-value count n/2−k−s≥n/4n/2-k-s\geq n/4 gives a bandwidth factor of ⌈log2⁡(n/4)/(H​m​p)⌉=⌈(log2⁡n−2)/(H​m​p)⌉\lceil\log_{2}(n/4)/(Hmp)\rceil=\lceil(\log_{2}n-2)/(Hmp)\rceil, matching Ω⁡(log2⁡n/(H​m​p))\Omega(\log_{2}n/(Hmp)) up to an additive O⁡(1)O(1) in the numerator. No log⁡s\log s loss appears in the distinct-value count. (The O⁡(H​log⁡s)O(H\log s) gap between Conjecture 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 is therefore attributable to the upper bound’s log2⁡(2​s)\log_{2}(2s) factor from windowed doubling’s inner loop, not to the lower-bound proof strategy.) In particular, Conjecture 3.1’s statement L=Ω⁡(⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉)L=\Omega(\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log n/(Hmp)\rceil) holds (modulo (⋆)(\star)) with a universal constant cc in the regime s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4.

Lemma 4.19 (Per-window cost).

For n≥4​kn\geq 4k, s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4, and a locality-respecting controller, any correct algorithm must satisfy ℓj−ℓj−1≥B−1\ell_{j}-\ell_{j-1}\geq B-1 for every j∈{1,…,W}j\in\{1,\dots,W\}, where

B:=⌈log2⁡nH​m​p⌉B\;:=\;\left\lceil\frac{\log_{2}n}{Hmp}\right\rceil

and ℓ0:=0\ell_{0}:=0. More precisely, B′:=ℓj−ℓj−1≥⌈log2⁡(⌊n/2⌋−k−s)/(H​m​p)⌉≥⌈(log2⁡n−2)/(H​m​p)⌉≥B−1B^{\prime}:=\ell_{j}-\ell_{j-1}\geq\lceil\log_{2}(\lfloor n/2\rfloor-k-s)/(Hmp)\rceil\geq\lceil(\log_{2}n-2)/(Hmp)\rceil\geq B-1; the additive −1-1 is O⁡(1)O(1) and is absorbed into the universal constant. No log2⁡s\log_{2}s loss appears.

Proof.

By Lemma 4.17, in the regime s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 there exist ℓ†\ell^{\dagger} and x†x^{\dagger} such that zτjz_{\tau_{j}} takes at least M:=⌊n/2⌋−k−s≥n/4M:=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-k-s\geq n/4 distinct values on Π†:={π:X0(ℓ†)​(π)=x†}\Pi^{\dagger}:=\{\pi:X^{(\ell^{\dagger})}_{0}(\pi)=x^{\dagger}\}, for n≥n0n\geq n_{0} sufficiently large. In case j≥2j\geq 2, ℓ†=ℓj−1\ell^{\dagger}=\ell_{j-1}; in case j=1j=1, ℓ†=0=ℓ0\ell^{\dagger}=0=\ell_{0}.

A correct algorithm maps each distinct zτjz_{\tau_{j}} to a distinct final query-token state (otherwise two inputs with different correct answers would produce the same output), so in particular at layer ℓj\ell_{j}, the representation X0(ℓj)X^{(\ell_{j})}_{0} must take at least MM distinct values on Π†\Pi^{\dagger}. By Lemma 4.2 with starting state x†x^{\dagger} and B′:=ℓj−ℓ†B^{\prime}:=\ell_{j}-\ell^{\dagger} layers of evolution,

M≤|ΣB′​(x†)|≤ 2B′​H​m​p,M\;\leq\;|\Sigma_{B^{\prime}}(x^{\dagger})|\;\leq\;2^{B^{\prime}Hmp},

which gives B′≥⌈log2⁡M/(H​m​p)⌉≥⌈(log2⁡n−2)/(H​m​p)⌉≥B−1B^{\prime}\geq\lceil\log_{2}M/(Hmp)\rceil\geq\lceil(\log_{2}n-2)/(Hmp)\rceil\geq B-1 where B:=⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉B:=\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil. Thus ℓj−ℓj−1≥B−1\ell_{j}-\ell_{j-1}\geq B-1 (with ℓ0=0\ell_{0}=0 for j=1j=1); the additive −1-1 is absorbed into the universal constant of Conjecture 3.1. ∎

Remark 4.20 (Dense regime n=O⁡(k)n=O(k)).

The adversarial construction of Lemma 4.17 requires n≥4​kn\geq 4k. In the dense regime n=O⁡(k)n=O(k), Proposition 4.4’s unconditional bound L≥max⁡(⌈(k−1)/s⌉,⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉)L\geq\max(\lceil(k-1)/s\rceil,\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil) still applies, giving L=Ω⁡(⌈k/s⌉)L=\Omega(\lceil k/s\rceil). The strengthening from ⌈(k−1)/s⌉\lceil(k-1)/s\rceil to ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil via Lemma 4.16 applies in the same s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 regime as Conjecture 3.1 (since Lemma 4.16’s proof also invokes the clean-target counting of Lemma 4.17); in particular, this unit-level strengthening requires the cycle-structure restriction and is not claimed for general ss.

Proof strategy for Conjecture 3.1, modulo (⋆)(\star).

Assuming the conclusion of Lemma 4.11 (exit exists at every window) and the regime n≥4​kn\geq 4k, s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4, we combine Lemma 4.16 and Lemma 4.19. Moreover, ℓj\ell_{j} is monotone in jj (since τj\tau_{j} is), so ℓ0≤ℓ1≤⋯≤ℓW≤L\ell_{0}\leq\ell_{1}\leq\cdots\leq\ell_{W}\leq L. With this definition, Lemma 4.16 gives ℓj⋅s≥τj\ell_{j}\cdot s\geq\tau_{j} (rephrased: at layer ℓj\ell_{j}, |Tℓj|≤1+ℓj​s|T_{\ell_{j}}|\leq 1+\ell_{j}s must be ≥τj+1\geq\tau_{j}+1, i.e., ℓj⋅s≥τj\ell_{j}\cdot s\geq\tau_{j}), and Lemma 4.19 gives ℓj−ℓj−1≥B−1\ell_{j}-\ell_{j-1}\geq B-1 where B:=⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉B:=\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil.

Now combine:

(a) Sequentiality (Lemma 4.16): ℓj⋅s≥τj\ell_{j}\cdot s\geq\tau_{j} for each jj; in particular ℓW≥W\ell_{W}\geq W when τW=k\tau_{W}=k.

(b) Per-window cost (Lemma 4.19): ℓj−ℓj−1≥B−1\ell_{j}-\ell_{j-1}\geq B-1 for each j∈{1,…,W}j\in\{1,\dots,W\}, where B:=⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉B:=\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil.

L≥ℓW=∑j=1W(ℓj−ℓj−1)≥W⋅(B−1)≥⌈ks⌉⋅⌈log2⁡nH​m​p⌉⋅(1−1B).L\;\geq\;\ell_{W}\;=\;\sum_{j=1}^{W}(\ell_{j}-\ell_{j-1})\;\geq\;W\cdot(B-1)\;\geq\;\left\lceil\frac{k}{s}\right\rceil\cdot\left\lceil\frac{\log_{2}n}{Hmp}\right\rceil\cdot\left(1-\frac{1}{B}\right).

For n≥n0:=100n\geq n_{0}:=100 (which ensures n/4≤n/16\sqrt{n}/4\leq n/16, hence k+s≤n/4+n/16≤n/3k+s\leq n/4+n/16\leq n/3, hence ⌊n/2⌋−k−s≥n/6≥n0/6≥16\lfloor n/2\rfloor-k-s\geq n/6\geq n_{0}/6\geq 16) and log2⁡n>H​m​p\log_{2}n>Hmp (so that B≥2B\geq 2; this is the condition for the bandwidth factor to be non-trivial—otherwise ⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉=1\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil=1 and the product bound reduces to cache reachability, already covered by Proposition 4.4), we have 1−1/B≥1/21-1/B\geq 1/2, yielding

L≥12⋅⌈ks⌉⋅⌈log2⁡nH​m​p⌉,L\;\geq\;\frac{1}{2}\cdot\left\lceil\frac{k}{s}\right\rceil\cdot\left\lceil\frac{\log_{2}n}{Hmp}\right\rceil,

i.e., Conjecture 3.1’s statement with c=1/2c=1/2. For s>n/4s>\sqrt{n}/4, the product-structure statement is not guaranteed by this proof strategy and we fall back to Proposition 4.4’s max-bound, as stipulated in the Conjecture 3.1 precondition.

The derivation uses the conclusion of Lemma 4.11 (existence of exit at every window); since Lemma 4.11 is left as Open Problem 1, this establishes Conjecture 3.1 modulo (⋆)(\star) rather than unconditionally. No log2⁡s\log_{2}s loss appears in this derivation: the clean-target counting of Lemma 4.17 reduces the set of valid reference permutations (via first-exit-step pigeonhole and cycle-structure restriction), but once a single valid π1\pi_{1} is fixed, the distinct-value count of zτjz_{\tau_{j}} is Ω⁡(n)\Omega(n) directly. ∎

Why the product (not max) bound holds.

The fact that each of the WW windows requires BB layers between resolutions, not just total, is what gives the product W⋅BW\cdot B rather than max⁡(W,B)\max(W,B). Lemma 4.19 is essential: window jj’s resolution cannot be pipelined within the BB layers devoted to window j−1j-1, because to distinguish among the Ω⁡(n/s)\Omega(n/s) possible values of zτjz_{\tau_{j}} requires BB fresh layers past ℓj−1\ell_{j-1}.

4.4 Remarks on Theorem 3.6

The proof of Theorem 3.6 was given in Section 3 following the theorem statement. Here we collect additional commentary on the barrier and the search for bypasses.

Remark 4.21 (Breaking the barrier).

Theorem 3.6 does not rule out lower bounds outside the class of Definition 3.5. Three natural avenues remain:

  1. 1.

    Unconditional communication-complexity lower bounds: the pointer chasing problem has been studied in multi-party communication models. Nisan and Wigderson (1993) proved a Ω~​(n/k2)\tilde{\Omega}(n/k^{2}) lower bound on the kk-round randomized communication complexity of kk-hop pointer chasing; (Yehudayoff, 2020) improved this to Ω~​(n/k−k​log⁡n)\tilde{\Omega}(n/k-k\log n), essentially matching Klauck’s earlier randomized lower bound and tight up to the k​log⁡nk\log n additive term relative to Nisan-Wigderson’s O~​(n/k)\tilde{O}(n/k) upper bound; (Mao et al., 2025) closed the remaining log⁡n\log n gap to Ω⁡(n/k+k)\Omega(n/k+k) via gadgetless lifting. These CC bounds are unconditional. What remains open is the lifting: translating such a CC bound into an unconditional Cache-Transformer depth lower bound without invoking (Sanford et al., 2024)’s MPC-conjecture reduction, which would bypass Definition 3.5.

  2. 2.

    Joint-state arguments: counting over the joint state (Xi(ℓ))i∈S(ℓ)(X^{(\ell)}_{i})_{i\in S^{(\ell)}} rather than the single state X0(ℓ)X^{(\ell)}_{0}. The joint state has capacity s​m​p>H​m​psmp>Hmp whenever s>Hs>H, potentially escaping the per-layer bandwidth limit. However, in the PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k} task only X0(L)X^{(L)}_{0} decodes to the output, so arguments coupling to joint cache states require additional task structure (e.g., requiring multiple output tokens or global statistics).

  3. 3.

    Information-theoretic multi-output tasks: tasks whose output is Ω⁡(H​m​p)\Omega(Hmp) bits (e.g., requiring Ω⁡(H​m​p/log⁡n)\Omega(Hmp/\log n) chain values as simultaneous outputs at layer LL) can give L≥log⁡(output)/(H​m​p)=Ω⁡(1)L\geq\log(\text{output})/(Hmp)=\Omega(1) from information alone. Such tasks deviate from PCn,k\mathrm{PC}_{n,k} as stated, but may be natural models of multi-hop reasoning in different settings.

Each of these is a distinct open problem.

Remark 4.22 (Exhaustive search for bypass arguments).

We considered eight alternative approaches to escape the barrier within counting-based arguments: (i) asymmetric rounds (parallel reasoning at multiple token positions); (ii) adversarial online streaming (cache commitment before seeing the rest of the input); (iii) query/cache capacity asymmetry (s​m​psmp vs m​pmp); (iv) counting distinguishability at non-query tokens; (v) pebbling-game time-space tradeoffs; (vi) direct-sum and XOR lemmas for independent task instances; (vii) communication-complexity fooling-set arguments, in particular round-elimination lower bounds for pointer chasing of the Duris et al. (1987) style; and (viii) average-case (random-π\pi) hardness. Each approach either saturates at ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil or yields a strictly weaker bound (e.g., (vii) via unconditional MPC bounds gives log⁡k/s\log k/s, weaker than k/sk/s for k≥2k\geq 2). We omit the detailed case-by-case analysis; the unified conclusion is the per-window structural limit formalized by Theorem 3.6.

4.5 Proof sketch of Theorem 3.2

Serial construction. At each of kk outer layers, the query token performs a single content-based lookup: its current slot encodes the current ztz_{t}, keys encode token identities ii, values encode payloads π⁡(i)\pi(i), and the attention output becomes the next zt+1z_{t+1}. Implementing one lookup requires O⁡(⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)O(\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil) sub-layers to encode/decode nn-ary pointers in mm-dimensional pp-bit vectors (standard construction, e.g., via binary decomposition). Total: L=O⁡(k⁡⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)L=O(k\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil).

Windowed pointer doubling. Partition the chain into W=⌈k/s⌉W=\lceil k/s\rceil windows of size ss each. Within each window, apply pointer doubling: at stage tt, compute π2t\pi^{2^{t}} on the window’s starting token using ⌈log2⁡s⌉\lceil\log_{2}s\rceil stages, so window jj consumes O⁡(⌈log2⁡s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)O(\lceil\log_{2}s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil) layers. Total: L=O⁡(⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)L=O(\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil). Take the minimum of the serial and windowed costs.

Fix π∼Unif⁡(Sn)\pi\sim\mathrm{Unif}(S_{n}). Let zt:=πt​(1)z_{t}:=\pi^{t}(1) for t≥0t\geq 0, with z0=1z_{0}=1. The cache at stage tt is Ct⊆[n]C_{t}\subseteq[n], |Ct|=s|C_{t}|=s. Success at stage tt is ℰt:={zt∈Ct}\mathcal{E}_{t}:=\{z_{t}\in C_{t}\}, joint success is ℰ:=∩t=1Tℰt\mathcal{E}:=\cap_{t=1}^{T}\mathcal{E}_{t}.

4.6.1 Oblivious case: exponential decay (Theorem 3.8)

The key idea is direct enumeration of (z1,…,zT)(z_{1},\dots,z_{T}) trajectories rather than a chain-rule decomposition. Because π\pi is uniform, any fixed distinct trajectory has probability (n−T)!/n!(n-T)!/n!; the joint hit event is a union over trajectories lying in C1×⋯×CTC_{1}\times\cdots\times C_{T}.

using n(n−1)⋯(n−T+1)≥(n−T+1)T≥(n−T)Tn(n-1)\cdots(n-T+1)\geq(n-T+1)^{T}\geq(n-T)^{T} for n≥T+1n\geq T+1.
