4.6.2 Adaptive case: upper bound (Theorem 3.9, upper bound)

The upper bound uses the fact that at stage 1, any locality-respecting controller’s cache C1C_{1} is independent of π⁡(1)\pi(1) (because C1C_{1} reads only positions in T0={0}T_{0}=\{0\}, which is disjoint from π\pi’s domain [n][n]).

Proof of Theorem 3.9, upper bound.

At stage 1, the trace T0={0}T_{0}=\{0\} (only the query token is accessible before any attention computation), so π|T0\pi|_{T_{0}} is vacuous. Hence C1C_{1} is a deterministic function of the empty string, i.e., constant. Therefore C1⟂πC_{1}\perp\pi, and since ℰ⊆ℰ1={π(1)∈C1}\mathcal{E}\subseteq\mathcal{E}_{1}=\{\pi(1)\in C_{1}\},

Pr[ℰ]≤Pr[π(1)∈C1]=|C1|n≤sn≤sn−T,\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\;\leq\;\Pr[\pi(1)\in C_{1}]\;=\;\frac{|C_{1}|}{n}\;\leq\;\frac{s}{n}\;\leq\;\frac{s}{n-T},

using that π⁡(1)\pi(1) is uniform on [n][n] under π∼Unif⁡(Sn)\pi\sim\mathrm{Unif}(S_{n}), |C1|≤s|C_{1}|\leq s, and n≥T+1n\geq T+1. ∎

4.6.3 Adaptive case: matching achievability (Theorem 3.9, lower bound)

We exhibit an explicit locality-respecting adaptive controller whose joint success probability matches the upper bound s/ns/n of Theorem 3.9 with exact equality. The strategy is “chain-tracking”: at stage 1, gamble s−1s-1 random slots plus the query’s source position 11 to learn π⁡(1)\pi(1); after a hit, the subsequent chain is deterministically known to the controller.

Proof of Theorem 3.9, lower bound.

Define the controller 𝖠⋆\mathsf{A}^{\star} as follows:

  • •

    Stage 1: C1={1,a1,a2,…,as−1}C_{1}=\{1,a_{1},a_{2},\dots,a_{s-1}\} for any fixed distinct ai∈[n]∖{1}a_{i}\in[n]\setminus\{1\}. Note 1∈C11\in C_{1}.

  • •

    Stage t≥2t\geq 2: If ℰ1,…,ℰt−1\mathcal{E}_{1},\dots,\mathcal{E}_{t-1} all occurred (stage t−1t-1 cache Ct−1∋zt−1C_{t-1}\ni z_{t-1}), then by induction z1,…,zt−1∈Tt−1z_{1},\dots,z_{t-1}\in T_{t-1}, and controller has read π\pi at these positions. In particular, controller knows zt=π⁡(zt−1)z_{t}=\pi(z_{t-1}). Set Ct∋ztC_{t}\ni z_{t} (other s−1s-1 slots arbitrary).

  • •

    If any earlier ℰi\mathcal{E}_{i} failed, set CtC_{t} arbitrarily (the joint event ℰ\mathcal{E} has already failed).

Locality check: At stage t≥2t\geq 2, CtC_{t} depends only on π|{1,z1,…,zt−1}⊆π|Tt−1\pi|_{\{1,z_{1},\dots,z_{t-1}\}}\subseteq\pi|_{T_{t-1}} (all indices in prior caches). Locality holds.

Success probability: Under 𝖠⋆\mathsf{A}^{\star}, if π⁡(1)∈C1\pi(1)\in C_{1} then stage 1 succeeds (z1=π⁡(1)∈C1=ℰ1z_{1}=\pi(1)\in C_{1}=\mathcal{E}_{1}), and the chain-tracking induction at subsequent stages deterministically maintains zt∈Ctz_{t}\in C_{t} for all t≥2t\geq 2: the controller has read π\pi at all previously-visited chain positions (including zt−1z_{t-1}), so it knows zt=π⁡(zt−1)z_{t}=\pi(z_{t-1}) and places it in CtC_{t}. This covers the fixed-point case π⁡(1)=1\pi(1)=1 as well: if π⁡(1)=1\pi(1)=1, the controller reads this at stage 1, knows zt=1z_{t}=1 for all tt, and includes 11 in every CtC_{t}, so ℰ\mathcal{E} holds. Therefore

Pr[ℰ]≥Pr[π(1)∈C1]=|C1|n=sn.\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\;\geq\;\Pr[\pi(1)\in C_{1}]\;=\;\frac{|C_{1}|}{n}\;=\;\frac{s}{n}.

This matches the upper bound s/ns/n of Theorem 3.9 exactly (both bounds are s/ns/n), giving Pr⁡[ℰ]=s/n\Pr[\mathcal{E}]=s/n. ∎

Proof of Corollary 3.10.

Adaptive achieves Pr⁡[ℰ]≥s/n\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\geq s/n (Theorem 3.9, achievability), while oblivious gives Pr⁡[ℰ]≤(s/(n−T))T+2​T3/n\Pr[\mathcal{E}]\leq(s/(n-T))^{T}+2T^{3}/n. 5 Architecture Comparison

Full attention’s depth scales as Ω⁡(k/s)\Omega(k/s) to O⁡((k/s)​log⁡s)O((k/s)\log s), with a gap of O⁡(log⁡s)O(\log s). Linear attention and RNNs are stuck at Θ⁡(k)\Theta(k) regardless of cache. Full attention’s advantage depends critically on cache size.

6 Experiments

We validate our bounds via constructive verification: we hardcode the serial pointer-chasing algorithm directly into Transformer weights and measure accuracy on random permutations. This eliminates optimization confounds entirely—success or failure reflects theoretical possibility, not SGD’s ability to find a solution.

6.1 Hardcoded Transformer (serial strategy)

We implement the serial strategy from Theorem 3.2’s proof as explicit Transformer weights on PC16,k\mathrm{PC}_{16,k}. Each layer performs one content-based lookup. We sweep k∈{1,2,4,8,12}k\in\{1,2,4,8,12\} and L∈{1,…,16}L\in\{1,\dots,16\} with 5000 random permutations per configuration. Results (Figure 1a): the transition from random guess (1/n=6.25%1/n=6.25\%) to 100%100\% is sharp at exactly L=kL=k.

6.2 Windowed pointer doubling vs. serial

We simulate oracle windowed pointer doubling on the same task, sweeping s∈{1,2,4,8,16}s\in\{1,2,4,8,16\}. Results (Figure 1b): for k=8k=8, serial requires L≥8L\geq 8, windowed PD with s=2s=2 achieves 100%100\% at L=4L=4, and s=8s=8 at L=3L=3. Cache size trades for depth, as predicted. Figure 2 shows the full depth–cache tradeoff with the O⁡(log⁡s)O(\log s) gap between lower bound and windowed PD visible.

6.3 Random cache: error amplification

Figure 1c shows that under oblivious (random) cache eviction, joint success probability decays sharply with kk. At s=8,n=16,k=8,T=3s=8,n=16,k=8,T=3, we observe empirical success of ≈17.5%\approx 17.5\%. The main term of Theorem 3.8’s upper bound is (s/(n−T))T=(8/13)3≈23.3%(s/(n-T))^{T}=(8/13)^{3}\approx 23.3\%, which upper-bounds the good-chain success probability Pr⁡[ℰgood]\Pr[\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{good}}] (not Pr⁡[ℰ]\Pr[\mathcal{E}] in general; the empirical 17.5%17.5\% includes contributions from ℰbad\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{bad}} not bounded by the main term alone). The main term matches the empirical value in order and confirms the qualitative (s/(n−T))T(s/(n-T))^{T} scaling. (The full theorem bound, including the 2​T3/n2T^{3}/n error term, exceeds 1 at this small nn; see Remark 3.12.) Note that the simpler expression (s/n)T=12.5%(s/n)^{T}=12.5\% underestimates because it uses nn rather than n−Tn-T in the denominator; Theorem 3.8 identifies the correct asymptotic decay rate as (s/(n−T))T(s/(n-T))^{T}, which reduces to (s/n)T​(1+O⁡(T2/n))(s/n)^{T}(1+O(T^{2}/n)) in the s/n→0s/n\to 0 regime.

6.4 Connection to LLM behavior

Ananthanarayanan et al. (2026) independently report a sharp hallucination cliff near 90% compression, with multi-hop (Hops) F1 dropping from ∼31%{\sim}31\% to near zero under aggressive compression, while single-hop retrieval degrades gracefully. This matches our framework qualitatively: kk-hop capability is gated by a product bound that involves kk, so multi-hop (k≥4k\geq 4) is hit harder than single-hop (k=1k=1) as ss shrinks. Liu et al. (2025) show that adaptive (heavy-hitter) eviction outperforms recency- and norm-based baselines on reasoning; Corollary 3.10 gives a direct quantitative explanation: adaptive controllers achieve Θ⁡(s/n)\Theta(s/n) joint success, while oblivious ones decay as (s/n)T(s/n)^{T}, a separation factor of Ω⁡((n/s)T−1)\Omega((n/s)^{T-1}). This is consistent with the observation that heavy-hitter-based methods, which concentrate cache on frequently-attended positions, provide qualitatively different error-scaling behavior than random or recency-based eviction. Caveat on regime. Our experiments at n=16,T=3n=16,T=3 do not fall within the “tight” regime of Corollary 3.10 (which requires s≥(2​T3)1/T⋅n(T−1)/T≈24s\geq(2T^{3})^{1/T}\cdot n^{(T-1)/T}\approx 24, exceeding n=16n=16); we view the empirical observations here as qualitative validation of the direction of the separation rather than quantitative confirmation of the (n/s)T−1(n/s)^{T-1} rate. Establishing the rate empirically in the main-term-dominates regime requires moderate-to-large nn (e.g., for s/n=1/2s/n=1/2 and T=3T=3, roughly n>432n>432; see Remark 3.12).

7 Related Work

Transformer depth.

Sanford et al. (2023) separated attention from RNNs via communication complexity. Sanford et al. (2024) proved Transformer–MPC equivalence. Alman and Yu (2025) gave SETH-conditional time bounds. Kozachinskiy et al. (2025) proved infinite-precision lower bounds. We introduce cache as a new parameter. Our finite-precision model is analogous to bounded-precision circuit models in computational complexity; the key distinction from (Sanford et al., 2024) is that their Ω⁡(log⁡k)\Omega(\log k) holds at infinite precision (conditional on MPC), while our conjectured product bound addresses the finite-precision regime (under a locality-respecting controller, which is satisfied by all standard KV-compression methods). The two results are complementary: neither implies the other.

KV cache compression.

Eviction: (Zhang et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Cai et al., 2024). Reasoning-specific: (Cai et al., 2025; Du et al., 2025). Empirical: (Liu et al., 2025; Ananthanarayanan et al., 2026). All heuristic/empirical; we provide the first formal depth–cache tradeoff for a stylized reasoning task.

Recent methods employ question-aware or position-aware scoring (pseudo-query-based selection, global per-head budget optimization, head-aware risk-adaptive gating). In our framework, such strategies correspond to smarter choices of the cache set S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)} within the locality-respecting class; they may improve constant factors in practice but are subject to the unconditional max-bound L=Ω⁡(max⁡(⌈k/s⌉,⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉))L=\Omega(\max(\lceil k/s\rceil,\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil)) (Proposition 4.4), and, if Conjecture 3.1 holds, cannot circumvent the product structure L=Ω⁡(⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉)L=\Omega(\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil). The locality assumption is satisfied by all practical methods. Systems that offload KV entries to slower storage and retrieve on demand effectively increase ss per layer (at latency cost), which our bounds correctly capture. Soft compression (vector quantization, value merging) reduces effective precision or merges tokens rather than evicting them; extending our counting argument to this setting is an open direction.

8 Discussion

We conjectured a product lower bound L=Ω⁡((k/s)⋅log⁡n/(H​m​p))L=\Omega((k/s)\cdot\log n/(Hmp)) (Conjecture 3.1) and isolated the sole remaining technical gap as the probabilistic step (⋆)(\star) in Remark 4.13. We unconditionally proved the max-bound L=Ω⁡(max⁡(⌈k/s⌉,⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉))L=\Omega(\max(\lceil k/s\rceil,\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil)) (Proposition 4.4), and an unconditional matching upper bound L=O⁡(⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡(2​s)⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(m​p)⌉)L=O(\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}(2s)\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(mp)\rceil) via windowed pointer doubling, so if Conjecture 3.1 holds then the characterization is tight up to O⁡(H​log⁡s)O(H\log s) in the narrow-model regime. We also proved unconditionally a bandwidth barrier showing that the product bound cannot be sharpened in the H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n regime by any per-window distinguishability-counting argument, and established that adaptive cache selection does not beat the oblivious bound at the first stage via a coupling argument. Theorems 3.8 and 3.9 (oblivious-vs-adaptive error behavior) are unconditional.

What the bandwidth barrier means.

Theorem 3.6 is the technically most significant structural statement of the paper. It explains a puzzling feature of existing cache-compression theory: why, despite decades of work on pointer chasing in communication complexity, we cannot get a depth lower bound for Transformers better than the trivial cache-reachability bound in the regime of practical interest. The barrier is that per-window output has log2⁡n\log_{2}n bits of “capacity” (since zτj∈[n]z_{\tau_{j}}\in[n]), while per-layer bandwidth is H​m​pHmp bits; the ratio ceilings at 11 whenever H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n. Breaking through requires either (i) output-informational arguments that escape the per-window output dimension (perhaps via multi-output tasks), (ii) translating the unconditional pointer-chasing CC lower bounds of (Nisan and Wigderson, 1993; Yehudayoff, 2020; Mao et al., 2025) into Cache-Transformer depth lower bounds without the MPC reduction (an open lifting problem), or (iii) joint-state counting that couples to cache-wide state capacity s​m​p>H​m​psmp>Hmp when s>Hs>H—but this in turn requires the task to force ss cache tokens to jointly carry information.

Limitations and scope.

Our model assumes hard cache boundaries, pp-bit precision, and a locality-respecting cache controller. The precision assumption is essential for Lemma 4.2 and reflects hardware reality. The locality assumption, which rules out controllers that examine representations outside the cache, is satisfied by all practical methods but is a genuine restriction relative to the most general adaptive controller. Our results thus complement (Sanford et al., 2024)’s infinite-precision, MPC-conditional Ω⁡(log⁡k)\Omega(\log k), which is cache-oblivious but holds under unrestricted computation. When s=ns=n (full cache), our bound gives only L≥⌈log⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉L\geq\lceil\log n/(Hmp)\rceil, weaker than Ω⁡(log⁡k)\Omega(\log k) but holding unconditionally on the controller.

In standard LLM configurations (large H​m​pHmp), the bandwidth factor equals 1, and our bound reduces to L≥⌈k/s⌉L\geq\lceil k/s\rceil alone—which holds unconditionally (without locality) via Lemma 4.1. The full product structure is a structural insight—cache and bandwidth are multiplicative, not competing—that becomes quantitatively binding in narrow or low-precision models.

Pointer chasing is a worst-case model; real reasoning tasks have exploitable structure permitting more aggressive compression than our bounds suggest. Our experiments use n=16n=16 for clarity; the hardcoded construction’s correctness is exact (independent of nn for n<2pn<2^{p}), so the sharp threshold behavior transfers to any nn within the precision range.

Concurrent work.

Ananthanarayanan et al. (2026) (arXiv March 2026) is a concurrent and independent empirical study. Their phase-transition-like behavior in multi-hop accuracy under compression is qualitatively consistent with our theory but was discovered independently.

Open problems.
  1. 1.

    Close the trace–chain joint-distribution gap in Lemma 4.11. The probabilistic step (⋆)(\star) in Remark 4.13—bounding Pr⁡[zσj​(π)∈T⁡(π)∣𝒟chain]≤𝔼⁡[|T|]/(n−1)\Pr[z_{\sigma_{j}}(\pi)\in T(\pi)\mid\mathcal{D}_{\text{chain}}]\leq\mathbb{E}[|T|]/(n-1), where σj:=τj−1\sigma_{j}:=\tau_{j}-1 is the chain position one step before window jj’s boundary—is left unproven for adaptive, label-sensitive algorithms under uniform π\pi. Two natural approaches: (a) a second-moment analysis using that the cycle structure of uniform π\pi decouples the orbit of 11 from other positions in a controlled way, or (b) a Yao-principle reduction against an explicit adversarial distribution on π\pi that directly implies the existence of a window-jj exit. Closing this single step would turn Conjecture 3.1 into a theorem (in the s≤n/4s\leq\sqrt{n}/4 regime).

  2. 2.

    Extend the product bound to the large-cache regime s>n/4s>\sqrt{n}/4. Our proof strategy for Conjecture 3.1 relies on restricting the reference permutation’s cycle structure (proof of Lemma 4.17), which degrades for s>n/4s>\sqrt{n}/4 and forces us to state the conjecture only in the complementary regime. In the large-cache regime we establish only the unconditional max-bound of Proposition 4.4. It is open whether the product structure ⌈k/s⌉⋅⌈log2⁡n/(H​m​p)⌉\lceil k/s\rceil\cdot\lceil\log_{2}n/(Hmp)\rceil continues to hold for s>n/4s>\sqrt{n}/4, or whether a different lower bound (e.g., a smooth interpolation between product and max in this range) is the truth.

  3. 3.

    Break the bandwidth barrier. Theorem 3.6 shows that any per-window distinguishability-based argument saturates at ⌈k/s⌉\lceil k/s\rceil when H​m​p≥log2⁡nHmp\geq\log_{2}n. Three avenues remain open: (i) translating the unconditional pointer-chasing CC lower bounds of (Nisan and Wigderson, 1993; Yehudayoff, 2020; Mao et al., 2025) into Cache-Transformer depth lower bounds without the MPC reduction, (ii) joint-state counting arguments coupling to cache-wide state capacity s​m​psmp rather than single-state m​pmp, (iii) information-theoretic lower bounds on multi-output reasoning tasks that require Ω⁡(H​m​p)\Omega(Hmp) bits per layer of coupled output.

  4. 4.

    Remove the locality restriction. Prove or disprove the product bound for fully adversarial cache controllers. Our adversarial construction (Lemma 4.14) uses locality to guarantee that perturbations outside T1T_{1} are invisible to the controller; one possible path is to show the controller can “leak” at most log2⁡(ns)\log_{2}\binom{n}{s} bits per layer via its S(ℓ)S^{(\ell)} choice, and to absorb this leakage into the bandwidth factor.

  5. 5.

    Close the O⁡(H​log⁡s)O(H\log s) gap between lower and upper bounds.

  6. 6.

    Extend the counting argument to soft compression (codebook size as effective bandwidth) and to infinite-precision models.

  7. 7.

    Extend Theorems 3.8 and 3.9 beyond the uniform-random π\pi assumption to structured or adversarial inputs, which is closer to the empirical setting where pointer chains are structured (e.g., by entity relations in language data). Our oblivious bound’s (s/(n−T))T(s/(n-T))^{T} decay rate depends on the uniformity of π\pi; under structured π\pi, both the oblivious decay rate and the adaptive-vs-oblivious separation may change.

  8. 8.

    Validate on NLP multi-hop benchmarks with trained Transformers.

  9. 9.

    Determine whether the product structure extends to reasoning tasks beyond pointer chasing, e.g., Boolean formula evaluation, tree-structured lookups, or graph reachability.
